  28def _soft_clamp(x: torch.Tensor, lo: torch.Tensor, hi: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
  29    """
  30    Soft (differentiable) clamp to the interval (lo, hi) using tanh.
  31
  32    Replaces torch.clamp, which has zero gradient outside [lo, hi] (dead-gradient
  33    problem: once n_raw overshoots the boundary, the optimizer has no signal to pull
  34    it back).
  35
  36    Mapping:  x_clamped = center + half * tanh(x / half)
  37      where center = (hi + lo) / 2  and  half = (hi - lo) / 2
  38
  39    Properties:
  40    - Linear (identity) for |x - center| << half  →  prior unchanged in typical range
  41    - Gradient = sech²(x/half) ≥ sech²(1) ≈ 0.42 at the "boundary" (|x| = half)
  42    - Gradient never reaches zero for finite x  →  no dead gradient
  43    - Asymptotes to ±half as |x| → ∞
  44    """
  45    half = 0.5 * (hi - lo)
  46    center = 0.5 * (hi + lo)
  47    return center + half * torch.tanh(x / half)

  53    def _save_checkpoint_atomic(self, checkpoint_path: str, data: dict) -> None:
  54        """Write checkpoint atomically (tmp → rename) and keep previous as .bak.
  55
  56        Three-step protocol:
  57          1. torch.save  →  <path>.tmp        (new data, not yet visible)
  58          2. os.replace  old <path>  →  .bak  (old data safely preserved)
  59          3. os.replace  .tmp  →  <path>      (atomic on POSIX; new data visible)
  60
  61        Failure modes:
  62          Die in step 1 (during write): .tmp corrupt, <path> unchanged → resume loads <path>.
  63          Die between 1 and 2: .tmp complete, <path> unchanged → resume loads <path>.
  64          Die between 2 and 3: .tmp complete, <path> gone (→ .bak) → resume tries .tmp
  65                                first (complete), falls back to .bak (one interval behind).
  66          Die during step 3:  os.replace is atomic on POSIX → either completes or not,
  67                              leaving either <path> or .tmp visible; .bak always intact.
  68        """
  69        backup_path = checkpoint_path + '.bak'
  70        tmp_path = checkpoint_path + '.tmp'
  71        torch.save(data, tmp_path)
  72        if os.path.exists(checkpoint_path):
  73            os.replace(checkpoint_path, backup_path)
  74        os.replace(tmp_path, checkpoint_path)

  98    def _tensor_summary(self, x: torch.Tensor):
  99        x_det = x.detach()
 100        finite = torch.isfinite(x_det)
 101        n = x_det.numel()
 102        n_bad = (~finite).sum().item()
 103        n_nan = torch.isnan(x_det).sum().item()
 104        n_inf = torch.isinf(x_det).sum().item()
 105        if finite.any():
 106            x_f = x_det[finite]
 107            mn = x_f.min().item()
 108            mx = x_f.max().item()
 109            mean = x_f.mean().item()
 110            std = x_f.std().item()
 111        else:
 112            mn = mx = mean = std = float("nan")
 113        return dict(n=n, n_bad=n_bad, n_nan=n_nan, n_inf=n_inf, min=mn, max=mx, mean=mean, std=std)
 114
 115    def _print_tensor(self, name: str, x: torch.Tensor, prefix=""):
 116        s = self._tensor_summary(x)
 117        print(
 118            f"{prefix}{name}: shape={tuple(x.shape)} dtype={x.dtype} device={x.device} "
 119            f"bad={s['n_bad']}/{s['n']} (nan={s['n_nan']}, inf={s['n_inf']}) "
 120            f"min={s['min']:.3g} max={s['max']:.3g} mean={s['mean']:.3g} std={s['std']:.3g}"
 121        )

 123    def _check_param_store_all(self, step: int, svi=None, where="", prev_finite=None, verbose_on_change=True):
 124        store = pyro.get_param_store()
 125        if prev_finite is None:
 126            prev_finite = {}
 127
 128        changed = []
 129        bad_vals = []
 130        bad_grads = []
 131
 132        for name, p in store.items():
 133            if not isinstance(p, torch.Tensor):
 134                continue
 135
 136            now_finite = torch.isfinite(p).all().item()
 137            was_finite = prev_finite.get(name, True)
 138            prev_finite[name] = now_finite
 139
 140            if was_finite and (not now_finite):
 141                changed.append(name)
 142
 143            if not now_finite:
 144                bad_vals.append(name)
 145
 146            if p.grad is not None and (not torch.isfinite(p.grad).all().item()):
 147                bad_grads.append(name)
 148
 149        if changed and verbose_on_change:
 150            print(f"\n[ERROR] Param(s) flipped finite→nonfinite at step {step} {where}: {changed}")
 151            for n in changed:
 152                self._print_tensor(n, store[n], prefix="  ")
 153                if store[n].grad is not None:
 154                    self._print_tensor(n + ".grad", store[n].grad, prefix="  ")
 155
 156        if bad_vals and verbose_on_change and not changed:
 157            print(f"\n[ERROR] Non-finite param value(s) present at step {step} {where}: "
 158                  f"{bad_vals[:10]}{'...' if len(bad_vals)>10 else ''}")
 159            for n in bad_vals[:10]:
 160                self._print_tensor(n, store[n], prefix="  ")
 161
 162        if bad_grads and verbose_on_change:
 163            print(f"\n[ERROR] Non-finite gradient(s) present at step {step} {where}: "
 164                  f"{bad_grads[:10]}{'...' if len(bad_grads)>10 else ''}")
 165            for n in bad_grads[:10]:
 166                if store[n].grad is not None:
 167                    self._print_tensor(n + ".grad", store[n].grad, prefix="  ")
 168
 169        # Best-effort optimizer-state check (optional)
 170        if svi is not None and hasattr(svi, "optim"):
 171            opt = svi.optim
 172            optim_objs = getattr(opt, "optim_objs", None)
 173            if isinstance(optim_objs, dict):
 174                bad_state = []
 175                for pname, torch_opt in optim_objs.items():
 176                    base_opt = getattr(torch_opt, "optimizer", torch_opt)
 177                    if not hasattr(base_opt, "state"):
 178                        continue
 179                    for group in base_opt.param_groups:
 180                        for param in group.get("params", []):
 181                            st = base_opt.state.get(param, {})
 182                            for key, val in st.items():
 183                                if torch.is_tensor(val) and (not torch.isfinite(val).all().item()):
 184                                    bad_state.append((pname, key))
 185                if bad_state and verbose_on_change:
 186                    print(f"\n[ERROR] Non-finite optimizer state at step {step} {where}: "
 187                          f"{bad_state[:10]}{'...' if len(bad_state)>10 else ''}")
 188
 189        any_bad = bool(bad_vals or bad_grads)
 190        return prev_finite, any_bad

 192    def _collect_dist_tensors(self, fn):
 193        tensors = []
 194        if isinstance(fn, dist.TransformedDistribution):
 195            tensors += self._collect_dist_tensors(fn.base_dist)
 196            return tensors
 197
 198        for attr in [
 199            "loc", "scale", "total_count", "logits", "probs", "rate",
 200            "concentration", "concentration0", "concentration1", "df"
 201        ]:
 202            if hasattr(fn, attr):
 203                v = getattr(fn, attr)
 204                if torch.is_tensor(v):
 205                    tensors.append((attr, v))
 206        return tensors

 208    def diagnose_nonfinite_sites(self, model, guide, *args, **kwargs):
 209        print("\n[DIAG] Running traced guide+model to locate non-finite site...")
 210
 211        guide_trace = poutine.trace(guide).get_trace(*args, **kwargs)
 212        replayed_model = poutine.replay(model, trace=guide_trace)
 213        model_trace = poutine.trace(replayed_model).get_trace(*args, **kwargs)
 214
 215        def scan_trace(tr, label):
 216            print(f"[DIAG] Scanning {label} trace...")
 217            for name, node in tr.nodes.items():
 218                if node.get("type") != "sample":
 219                    continue
 220
 221                fn = node["fn"]
 222                val = node["value"]
 223
 224                if torch.is_tensor(val) and (not torch.isfinite(val).all().item()):
 225                    print(f"  [BAD VALUE] site={name}")
 226                    self._print_tensor(f"{label}:{name}.value", val, prefix="    ")
 227                    return name
 228
 229                for attr, ten in self._collect_dist_tensors(fn):
 230                    if not torch.isfinite(ten).all().item():
 231                        print(f"  [BAD DIST PARAM] site={name} param={attr}")
 232                        self._print_tensor(f"{label}:{name}.fn.{attr}", ten, prefix="    ")
 233                        return name
 234
 235                if "log_prob" in node:
 236                    lp = node["log_prob"]
 237                    if torch.is_tensor(lp) and (not torch.isfinite(lp).all().item()):
 238                        print(f"  [BAD LOG_PROB] site={name}")
 239                        self._print_tensor(f"{label}:{name}.log_prob", lp, prefix="    ")
 240                        return name
 241
 242            print(f"[DIAG] No non-finite sample sites found in {label} trace.")
 243            return None
 244
 245        bad_guide = scan_trace(guide_trace, "guide")
 246        bad_model = scan_trace(model_trace, "model")
 247        print(f"[DIAG] First bad site guide={bad_guide} model={bad_model}\n")
 248
 249    def _debug_svi_step(self, svi, step, prev_finite, *args, **kwargs):
 250        """
 251        A 'manual' SVI step that lets us check:
 252          - pre-step params
 253          - post-grads, pre-update params/grads
 254          - post-update params
 255        and run trace diagnosis on first failure.
 256        """
 257        # Pre-step check
 258        prev_finite, any_bad = self._check_param_store_all(
 259            step, svi=svi, where="(pre-step)", prev_finite=prev_finite
 260        )
 261        if any_bad:
 262            store = pyro.get_param_store()
 263            if "locs.log_K_a" in store and store["locs.log_K_a"].grad is not None:
 264                g = store["locs.log_K_a"].grad
 265                bad_idx = torch.nonzero(torch.isnan(g), as_tuple=False).squeeze(-1)
 266                if bad_idx.numel() > 0:
 267                    self._diagnose_log_Ka_nan_grad(svi, bad_idx, *args, **kwargs)
 268        
 269            self.diagnose_nonfinite_sites(svi.model, svi.guide, *args, **kwargs)
 270            raise FloatingPointError("Non-finite grads/params after loss_and_grads (before update).")
 271
 272
 273        # Compute loss + grads (no update yet)
 274        with poutine.trace(param_only=True) as param_capture:
 275            loss = svi.loss_and_grads(svi.model, svi.guide, *args, **kwargs)
 276
 277        # Post-grads check (this often catches the real cause)
 278        prev_finite, any_bad = self._check_param_store_all(
 279            step, svi=svi, where="(post-grads, pre-update)", prev_finite=prev_finite
 280        )
 281        if any_bad:
 282            store = pyro.get_param_store()
 283            if "locs.log_K_a" in store and store["locs.log_K_a"].grad is not None:
 284                g = store["locs.log_K_a"].grad
 285                bad_idx = torch.nonzero(torch.isnan(g), as_tuple=False).squeeze(-1)
 286                if bad_idx.numel() > 0:
 287                    self._diagnose_log_Ka_nan_grad(svi, bad_idx, *args, **kwargs)
 288            self.diagnose_nonfinite_sites(svi.model, svi.guide, *args, **kwargs)
 289            # Fitting will stop: FloatingPointError is caught in the main loop → [STOP] + break
 290            raise FloatingPointError("Non-finite grads/params after loss_and_grads (before update).")
 291
 292        # Apply optimizer update
 293        params = set(site["value"].unconstrained() for site in param_capture.trace.nodes.values())
 294        svi.optim(params)
 295
 296        # Post-update check
 297        prev_finite, any_bad = self._check_param_store_all(
 298            step, svi=svi, where="(post-update)", prev_finite=prev_finite
 299        )
 300        if any_bad:
 301            store = pyro.get_param_store()
 302            if "locs.log_K_a" in store and store["locs.log_K_a"].grad is not None:
 303                g = store["locs.log_K_a"].grad
 304                bad_idx = torch.nonzero(torch.isnan(g), as_tuple=False).squeeze(-1)
 305                if bad_idx.numel() > 0:
 306                    self._diagnose_log_Ka_nan_grad(svi, bad_idx, *args, **kwargs)
 307            self.diagnose_nonfinite_sites(svi.model, svi.guide, *args, **kwargs)
 308            # Fitting will stop: FloatingPointError is caught in the main loop → [STOP] + break
 309            raise FloatingPointError("Optimizer update produced non-finite params.")
 310
 311        return loss, prev_finite

 313    def _diagnose_log_Ka_nan_grad(self, svi, bad_idx, *args, **kwargs):
 314        """
 315        bad_idx: 1D LongTensor of indices where locs.log_K_a.grad is NaN
 316        Prints model/guide site values for those indices and derived quantities
 317        (phi, Hill logit range, NB logits range).
 318        """
 319        import pyro.poutine as poutine
 320        import torch
 321    
 322        print(f"\n[DIAG+] NaN grad indices for log_K_a: {bad_idx.tolist()}")
 323    
 324        guide_trace = poutine.trace(svi.guide).get_trace(*args, **kwargs)
 325        replayed_model = poutine.replay(svi.model, trace=guide_trace)
 326        model_trace = poutine.trace(replayed_model).get_trace(*args, **kwargs)
 327    
 328        def get_site(tr, name):
 329            return tr.nodes[name]["value"] if name in tr.nodes else None
 330    
 331        # --- pull site values (all should be finite, but may be extreme) ---
 332        def _first_nonnone(*vals):
 333            return next((v for v in vals if v is not None), None)
 334        log_K_a = _first_nonnone(get_site(model_trace, "log_K_a"), get_site(guide_trace, "log_K_a"))
 335        log_Vmax_a = _first_nonnone(get_site(model_trace, "log_Vmax_a"), get_site(guide_trace, "log_Vmax_a"))
 336        Vmax_a = get_site(model_trace, "Vmax_a")
 337        K_a = get_site(model_trace, "K_a")
 338        n_a = get_site(model_trace, "n_a")
 339        A = get_site(model_trace, "A")
 340        o_y = get_site(model_trace, "o_y")  # sampled per feature
 341        alpha = get_site(model_trace, "alpha")  # relaxed bernoulli
 342    
 343        # Some of these might not exist depending on branch / naming
 344        for name, tensor in [
 345            ("log_K_a", log_K_a),
 346            ("K_a", K_a),
 347            ("log_Vmax_a", log_Vmax_a),
 348            ("Vmax_a", Vmax_a),
 349            ("n_a", n_a),
 350            ("A", A),
 351            ("o_y", o_y),
 352            ("alpha", alpha),
 353        ]:
 354            if tensor is None:
 355                continue
 356            sel = tensor[bad_idx]
 357            self._print_tensor(f"{name}[bad_idx]", sel, prefix="  ")
 358    
 359        # --- derived phi and ranges (very informative) ---
 360        if o_y is not None:
 361            phi = 1.0 / (o_y ** 2)
 362            self._print_tensor("phi_y[bad_idx]", phi[bad_idx], prefix="  ")
 363    
 364        # --- derived Hill logit range (this catches x**n instabilities) ---
 365        # kwargs must include x_true_sample, and we prefer to use log_K_a directly
 366        x_true = kwargs.get("x_true_sample", None)
 367        if x_true is not None and log_K_a is not None and n_a is not None:
 368            tiny = torch.finfo(x_true.dtype).tiny
 369            log_x = torch.log(x_true.clamp_min(tiny)).unsqueeze(-1)  # [N,1]
 370            # logit for each bad feature: [N, |bad_idx|]
 371            logit = (n_a[bad_idx].unsqueeze(0) * (log_x - log_K_a[bad_idx].unsqueeze(0)))
 372            # print range across cells (per bad feature)
 373            logit_min = logit.min(dim=0).values
 374            logit_max = logit.max(dim=0).values
 375            self._print_tensor("hill_logit_min[bad_idx]", logit_min, prefix="  ")
 376            self._print_tensor("hill_logit_max[bad_idx]", logit_max, prefix="  ")
 377    
 378            # approximate Hill output range
 379            if Vmax_a is not None:
 380                H = Vmax_a[bad_idx].unsqueeze(0) * torch.sigmoid(logit)
 381                self._print_tensor("Hilla_min[bad_idx]", H.min(dim=0).values, prefix="  ")
 382                self._print_tensor("Hilla_max[bad_idx]", H.max(dim=0).values, prefix="  ")
 383    
 384        # --- derived NB logits range for bad features (if you pass mu_y pieces) ---
 385        # We can’t see mu_final unless you expose it; but we can at least compute the part driven by Hill:
 386        # If you want full mu_final, expose it via pyro.deterministic (recommended).
 387        print("[DIAG+] If hill_logit range is extreme (e.g. > ~80 in magnitude), Hill math/backward is a prime suspect.\n")
 388

 391    ## Step 3: Fit trans effects (model_y) ##
 392    #########################################
 393    def _model_y(
 394        self,
 395        N,
 396        T,
 397        y_obs_tensor,
 398        sum_factor_tensor,
 399        beta_o_alpha_tensor,
 400        beta_o_beta_tensor,
 401        K_max_tensor,
 402        K_alpha_tensor,
 403        Vmax_mean_tensor,
 404        Vmax_alpha_tensor,
 405        n_mu_tensor,
 406        Amean_tensor,
 407        p_n_logits_tensor,
 408        epsilon_tensor,
 409        x_true_sample,
 410        nmin,
 411        nmax,
 412        alpha_y_sample=None,
 413        C=None,
 414        groups_tensor=None,
 415        temperature=1.0,
 416        use_straight_through=False,
 417        function_type='single_hill',
 418        polynomial_degree=6,
 419        use_alpha=True,
 420        distribution='negbinom',
 421        denominator_tensor=None,
 422        K=None,
 423        x_true_CV=None,
 424        x_ntc_mean=None,
 425        use_epsilon=True,
 426        vmax_log_sigma_floor_tensor=None,
 427        k_log_sigma_min_tensor=None,
 428        k_center_tensor=None,
 429        y_ntc_tensor=None,
 430        mean_y_corrected_tensor=None,
 431        o_y_ntc_tensor=None,
 432        sigma_hat_tensor=None,
 433        alpha_n_coupling: float = 10.0,
 434        latents_only=False,
 435    ):
 436
 437        if use_alpha:
 438            alpha_dist = dist.RelaxedBernoulliStraightThrough if use_straight_through else dist.RelaxedBernoulli
 439
 440        trans_plate = pyro.plate("trans_plate", T, dim=-1)
 441        
 442        ##########
 443        ## x_true (Now Fully Observed) ##
 444        ##########
 445        x_true = x_true_sample
 446    
 447        ####################
 448        ## alpha_y ##
 449        ####################
 450        alpha_y = None
 451        if alpha_y_sample is not None:
 452            alpha_y = alpha_y_sample
 453    
 454        ##############################################
 455        ## Feature-level variance (distribution-specific)
 456        ##############################################
 457        phi_y_used = None  # NB dispersion; None for other distributions
 458        sigma_y    = None  # noise scale for normal/studentt
 459
 460        if distribution == 'negbinom':
 461            beta_o = pyro.sample("beta_o", dist.Gamma(beta_o_alpha_tensor, beta_o_beta_tensor))
 462            with trans_plate:
 463                o_y = pyro.sample("o_y", dist.Exponential(beta_o))
 464                phi_y = 1 / (o_y**2)
 465            phi_y_used = phi_y.unsqueeze(-2)
 466            # A-prior weight: noisier genes get stronger pull toward NTC anchor.
 467            # Use NTC-estimated o_y when available (sampled o_y is near-unidentifiable
 468            # in fit_trans, so its posterior stays close to the prior mean for all genes).
 469            _prior_mean_o_y = (beta_o_beta_tensor / beta_o_alpha_tensor).clamp_min(epsilon_tensor)
 470            if o_y_ntc_tensor is not None:
 471                _o_y_weight = o_y_ntc_tensor / (o_y_ntc_tensor + _prior_mean_o_y)  # [T], fixed
 472            else:
 473                _o_y_weight = o_y / (o_y + _prior_mean_o_y)  # [T], sampled (fallback)
 474
 475        elif distribution in ('normal', 'studentt'):
 476            with trans_plate:
 477                if sigma_hat_tensor is not None:
 478                    sigma_y = pyro.sample("sigma_y", dist.HalfNormal(2.0 * sigma_hat_tensor))
 479                    # A-prior weight: features with larger NTC sigma pulled more toward NTC anchor.
 480                    _sigma_ref = sigma_hat_tensor.mean().clamp_min(epsilon_tensor)
 481                    _o_y_weight = sigma_hat_tensor / (sigma_hat_tensor + _sigma_ref)  # [T], fixed
 482                else:
 483                    sigma_y = pyro.sample("sigma_y", dist.HalfCauchy(self._t(10.0)))
 484                    _o_y_weight = self._t(0.5)  # neutral without NTC data
 485
 486        else:  # binomial, multinomial — variance fully determined by count totals
 487            _o_y_weight = self._t(0.5)  # neutral; no per-feature noise parameter
 488
 489        # Degrees of freedom: Student-t only, fixed at 3 to match fit_ntc
 490        nu_y = self._t(3.0) if distribution == 'studentt' else None
 491    
 492        #################
 493        ## Hill-based: ##
 494        #################
 495        if function_type in ['polynomial']:
 496            #sigma_coeff = pyro.sample("sigma_coeff", dist.Exponential(100)) #   -> controls how variable n_a can be across genes
 497            sigma_coeff = pyro.sample("sigma_coeff", dist.HalfCauchy(scale=self._t(1.0)))
 498        
 499        # Now enter the trans_plate (T dimension)
 500        with trans_plate:
 501
 502            # For multinomial, Amean_tensor and Vmax_mean_tensor are already [T, K] shaped
 503            # For binomial, they are [T] shaped
 504            # We keep them in their native shape for per-category priors in multinomial
 505
 506            # Baseline parameter A depends on distribution:
 507            # - normal/studentt: can be negative (natural value space)
 508            # - negbinom: positive count
 509            # - binomial/multinomial: probability in [0,1], using NEW reparameterization
 510            if distribution in ['normal', 'studentt']:
 511                # A prior: NTC-anchored Normal (analogous to negbinom LogNormal, but in linear
 512                # space since normal/studentt values can be negative).
 513                #
 514                # When y_ntc available (fit_ntc has been run):
 515                #   w → 0 (quiet feature): prior centred at Amean; y_ntc is 1σ above
 516                #   w → 1 (noisy feature): prior centred at y_ntc
 517                #   sigma = |y_ntc − Amean| floored at 10% of response amplitude
 518                #
 519                # Fallback (no NTC posterior): fixed-shift approach using response amplitude.
 520                delta_A = (Vmax_mean_tensor - Amean_tensor).clamp_min(epsilon_tensor)
 521                if y_ntc_tensor is not None:
 522                    sigma_A = (y_ntc_tensor - Amean_tensor).abs().clamp_min(delta_A * 0.1)
 523                    mean_A  = (1.0 - _o_y_weight) * Amean_tensor + _o_y_weight * y_ntc_tensor
 524                else:
 525                    sigma_A = delta_A
 526                    _shift_A = (1.0 - _o_y_weight) * 0.55
 527                    mean_A  = Amean_tensor - _shift_A * delta_A
 528                A = pyro.sample("A", dist.Normal(mean_A, sigma_A))
 529
 530            elif distribution in ['binomial', 'multinomial']:
 531                # Beta/Dirichlet priors for bounded [0, 1] likelihoods.
 532                # For binomial:    A ~ Beta(1, β) with mean = 0.5×Q05
 533                # For multinomial: A ~ Dirichlet with mean = 0.5×Q05 (row-normalized)
 534                #
 535                # POTENTIAL IMPROVEMENT: noise-adaptive shift (not yet implemented).
 536                # Analogous to the o_y weighting for negbinom/normal/studentt, the A prior
 537                # shift could be attenuated for low-coverage features where PSI estimates
 538                # are unreliable. The natural noise proxy is mean denominator read depth:
 539                #   _binom_weight = n_ref / (n_ref + mean_denom)   ∈ (0, 1)
 540                #   shift = 0.5 * (1 - _binom_weight)              (0.5 → 0 as reads increase)
 541                # where mean_denom = obs_denom.mean(cells) for binomial, or
 542                # obs_counts.sum(categories).mean(cells) for multinomial.
 543                # A data-adaptive n_ref = median(mean_denom) across features would be
 544                # more principled than a fixed count threshold.
 545
 546                # Amean_tensor: [T] for binomial, [T, K] for multinomial
 547                # Vmax_mean_tensor: [T] for binomial, [T, K] for multinomial
 548
 549                # Sample A
 550                if distribution == 'multinomial' and Amean_tensor.ndim > 1:
 551                    # For multinomial: LogisticNormal prior on A (Normal in logit space + softmax).
 552                    #
 553                    # We previously used dist.Dirichlet, but Pyro's autoguide represents the
 554                    # K-simplex via a stick-breaking transform from R^(K-1).  With K=65 and
 555                    # many phantom (all-zero) categories, float32 rounding in the stick-breaking
 556                    # product chain makes the sample sum drift away from 1.0 beyond PyTorch's
 557                    # 1e-6 Simplex tolerance, raising a ValueError in both compute_log_prob and
 558                    # compute_score_parts — even with validate_args=False on the model, the
 559                    # guide's TransformedDistribution re-validates the same sample.
 560                    #
 561                    # LogisticNormal sidesteps this entirely: the guide uses an unconstrained
 562                    # Normal site (no simplex constraint, no stick-breaking), and softmax
 563                    # guarantees a valid probability vector in the model.
 564                    K_dim = Amean_tensor.shape[-1]
 565
 566                    # Build phantom mask (categories with zero observations across all cells)
 567                    phantom_conc_mask = None
 568                    if y_obs_tensor.dim() == 3:  # multinomial: [N, T, K]
 569                        obs_total = y_obs_tensor.sum(dim=0)  # [T, K]
 570                        phantom_conc_mask = (obs_total == 0)  # [T, K]
 571
 572                    # Logit-space prior mean (base: from Q05)
 573                    A_mean_clamped = (0.5 * Amean_tensor).clamp(min=epsilon_tensor, max=1.0 - epsilon_tensor)
 574                    A_mean_normalized = A_mean_clamped / A_mean_clamped.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)  # [T, K]
 575                    A_logit_mean_base = torch.log(A_mean_normalized.clamp(min=1e-10))              # [T, K]
 576
 577                    # A prior: w-interpolated LogisticNormal anchored between data-driven
 578                    # lower anchor and y_ntc. Mode at (1-w)*A_logit_mean_base + w*logit(y_ntc),
 579                    # where w = o_y_ntc / (o_y_ntc + prior_mean_o_y).
 580                    if y_ntc_tensor is not None:
 581                        if y_ntc_tensor.ndim != 2 or y_ntc_tensor.shape[0] != T or y_ntc_tensor.shape[1] != K_dim:
 582                            raise ValueError(
 583                                f"y_ntc_tensor shape {tuple(y_ntc_tensor.shape)} does not match "
 584                                f"expected multinomial shape [{T}, {K_dim}]."
 585                            )
 586                        logit_y_ntc       = torch.log(y_ntc_tensor.clamp(min=1e-10))      # [T, K], log-simplex
 587                        A_logit_mean_base = torch.maximum(A_logit_mean_base, logit_y_ntc - 4.0)
 588                        w_expanded        = _o_y_weight.unsqueeze(-1)                      # [T, 1]
 589                        A_logit_mean      = (1.0 - w_expanded) * A_logit_mean_base + w_expanded * logit_y_ntc  # [T, K]
 590                        sigma_A_logit     = (logit_y_ntc - A_logit_mean_base).abs().clamp_min(1.0)             # [T, K]
 591                    else:
 592                        A_logit_mean  = A_logit_mean_base
 593                        sigma_A_logit = self._t(1.0)
 594
 595                    # Push phantom categories to -inf in prior mean so the guide learns
 596                    # to assign them zero probability.
 597                    if phantom_conc_mask is not None:
 598                        A_logit_mean = A_logit_mean.masked_fill(phantom_conc_mask, -1e4)
 599
 600                    # Sample in unconstrained logit space — no simplex constraint, no stick-breaking.
 601                    A_logit = pyro.sample("A", dist.Normal(A_logit_mean, sigma_A_logit).to_event(1))  # [T, K]
 602
 603                    # Softmax with phantom masking → valid probability vector [T, K]
 604                    if phantom_conc_mask is not None:
 605                        A_logit = A_logit.masked_fill(phantom_conc_mask, -1e9)
 606                    A = torch.softmax(A_logit, dim=-1)  # [T, K]
 607
 608                else:
 609                    # For binomial: Logit-Normal prior when y_ntc available (analogous to negbinom
 610                    # LogNormal, adapted to the [0,1] simplex via logit transform).
 611                    #
 612                    # When y_ntc available:
 613                    #   Lower anchor: logit(Amean/2); upper anchor: logit(y_ntc)
 614                    #   w → 0 (quiet feature): centred at logit(Amean/2); y_ntc is 1σ above
 615                    #   w → 1 (noisy feature): centred at logit(y_ntc)
 616                    #   sigma = (logit(y_ntc) − logit(Amean/2)).clamp_min(1 logit unit)
 617                    #
 618                    # Fallback (no NTC posterior): Beta(1, β) with mean = 0.5×Q05.
 619                    if y_ntc_tensor is not None:
 620                        # Lift upper anchor to mean(y_corrected) when y_ntc < mean.
 621                        if mean_y_corrected_tensor is not None:
 622                            effective_y_ntc = torch.maximum(y_ntc_tensor, mean_y_corrected_tensor)
 623                        else:
 624                            effective_y_ntc = y_ntc_tensor
 625                        logit_Amean_half = torch.logit((0.5 * Amean_tensor).clamp(1e-6, 1.0 - 1e-6))      # [T]
 626                        logit_y_ntc      = torch.logit(effective_y_ntc.clamp(1e-6, 1.0 - 1e-6))            # [T]
 627                        logit_Amean_half = torch.maximum(logit_Amean_half, logit_y_ntc - 4.0)              # cap: sigma ≤ 4
 628                        sigma_logit = (logit_y_ntc - logit_Amean_half).clamp_min(1.0)                      # [T]
 629                        mu_logit    = (1.0 - _o_y_weight) * logit_Amean_half + _o_y_weight * logit_y_ntc  # [T]
 630                        logit_A = pyro.sample("logit_A", dist.Normal(mu_logit, sigma_logit))            # [T]
 631                        A = pyro.deterministic("A", torch.sigmoid(logit_A))                             # [T]
 632                    else:
 633                        A_mean_shifted = (0.5 * Amean_tensor).clamp_min(epsilon_tensor)
 634                        beta_A = (1.0 - A_mean_shifted) / A_mean_shifted                               # [T]
 635                        A = pyro.sample("A", dist.Beta(self._t(1.0), beta_A).expand([T]))              # [T]
 636
 637            else:
 638                # For negbinom: LogNormal A prior (Normal in log2 space) with noise-adaptive mean.
 639                # log2(A) ~ Normal(mu_log2_A, sigma_log2_A), so A = 2^log2(A).
 640                #
 641                # mu_log2_A interpolates in log2 space between two gene-specific anchors:
 642                #   w → 0 (quiet gene, informative likelihood): log2(Amean/2)
 643                #   w → 1 (noisy gene, weak likelihood):        log2(y_ntc)
 644                #
 645                # sigma_log2_A = log2(y_ntc) - lower_anchor, floored at 1 octave, capped at 4.
 646                if y_ntc_tensor is not None:
 647                    log2_y_ntc = torch.log2(y_ntc_tensor)
 648                    # Lift upper anchor to mean(y_corrected) when y_ntc < mean — prevents
 649                    # both anchors collapsing to the floor for genes absent in NTC but
 650                    # expressed in perturbed conditions.
 651                    if mean_y_corrected_tensor is not None:
 652                        log2_upper_anchor = torch.maximum(log2_y_ntc, torch.log2(mean_y_corrected_tensor))
 653                    else:
 654                        log2_upper_anchor = log2_y_ntc
 655                    log2_Amean_half = torch.maximum(
 656                        torch.log2(Amean_tensor / 2.0),
 657                        log2_upper_anchor - 4.0,
 658                    )
 659                    sigma_log2_A = (log2_upper_anchor - log2_Amean_half).clamp_min(1.0)  # ≤ 4 octaves
 660                    mu_log2_A    = (1.0 - _o_y_weight) * log2_Amean_half + _o_y_weight * log2_upper_anchor
 661                else:
 662                    log2_Amean_half = torch.log2(Amean_tensor / 2.0)
 663                    sigma_log2_A    = self._t(4.0)
 664                    mu_log2_A       = log2_Amean_half
 665                log2_A = pyro.sample("log2_A", dist.Normal(mu_log2_A, sigma_log2_A))
 666                A = pyro.deterministic("A", torch.pow(self._t(2.0), log2_A))
 667
 668            if use_alpha:
 669                # Relaxed Bernoulli: alpha ~ (0,1), becomes more discrete as temperature -> 0
 670                # For multinomial: per-category gate — each of the K-1 categories can
 671                # independently be "on" or "off". This allows, e.g., only one acceptor to
 672                # respond while others remain flat. The Kth (residual) category is affected
 673                # iff at least one K-1 category is on (conservation of probability).
 674                if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 675                    alpha = pyro.sample("alpha", alpha_dist(temperature=temperature, logits=p_n_logits_tensor).expand([K - 1]).to_event(1))  # [T, K-1]
 676                else:
 677                    alpha = pyro.sample("alpha", alpha_dist(temperature=temperature, logits=p_n_logits_tensor))  # [T]
 678            else:
 679                if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 680                    alpha = torch.ones((T, K - 1), device=self.model.device)
 681                else:
 682                    alpha = torch.ones((T,), device=self.model.device)
 683            
 684            if function_type in ['single_hill', 'additive_hill', 'nested_hill']:
 685
 686                #####################################
 687                ## function priors (depend on o_y) ##
 688                #####################################
 689                # Gamma and delta depend on T dimension
 690                # Reduce over group dimension if necessary
 691                K_sigma = (K_max_tensor / (self._t(2) * torch.sqrt(K_alpha_tensor))) + epsilon_tensor
 692
 693                # For multinomial, reduce [T, K] → [T] for the Hill function amplitude prior
 694                # For other distributions, use Vmax_mean_tensor directly
 695                if distribution == 'multinomial' and Vmax_mean_tensor.ndim > 1:
 696                    Vmax_prior_mean = Vmax_mean_tensor.mean(dim=-1)  # [T]
 697                else:
 698                    Vmax_prior_mean = Vmax_mean_tensor  # [T]
 699
 700                Vmax_sigma = (Vmax_prior_mean / torch.sqrt(Vmax_alpha_tensor)) + epsilon_tensor
 701
 702                # Compute the unconstrained prior mean for n_raw that maps to n_mu under
 703                # soft_clamp.  Without this correction, Normal(0, sigma) on n_raw has its
 704                # constrained mode at center_n = (nmin + nmax)/2, which can be far from 0
 705                # when nmin/nmax are asymmetric (e.g. all x > 1 → nmin = −100, center ≈ −31).
 706                _center_n = 0.5 * (nmax + nmin)
 707                _half_n   = 0.5 * (nmax - nmin).clamp_min(epsilon_tensor)
 708                _ratio_n  = ((n_mu_tensor - _center_n) / _half_n).clamp(-1 + 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)
 709                n_mu_raw_tensor = _half_n * torch.atanh(_ratio_n)
 710
 711                # Per-gene n scale: sampled inside trans_plate so each gene is
 712                # independently regularised (prevents one noisy gene from inflating
 713                # the global sigma and loosening the prior for all other genes).
 714                sigma_n_a = pyro.sample("sigma_n_a", dist.Exponential(self._t(1.0)))
 715
 716                # For multinomial, we need per-category parameters (K-1 categories, Kth is residual)
 717                if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 718                    K_minus_1 = K - 1
 719                    # Sample parameters for K-1 categories
 720                    # Each category gets its own Hill function parameters
 721                    # Use .to_event(1) instead of a nested plate to avoid dim=-1 collision with trans_plate
 722                    n_a_raw = pyro.sample("n_a_raw", dist.Normal(n_mu_raw_tensor, sigma_n_a.unsqueeze(-1).expand(T, K_minus_1)).to_event(1))  # [T, K-1]
 723                    n_a = pyro.deterministic(
 724                        "n_a",
 725                        _soft_clamp(n_a_raw, nmin, nmax)
 726                    )  # [T, K-1]
 727                else:
 728                    # For non-multinomial: single set of parameters per feature
 729                    n_a_raw = pyro.sample("n_a_raw", dist.Normal(n_mu_raw_tensor, sigma_n_a))
 730                    n_a = pyro.deterministic(
 731                        "n_a",
 732                        _soft_clamp(n_a_raw, nmin, nmax)
 733                    )
 734
 735                # Identifiability coupling: when n_a≈0 the Hill is flat and alpha·Vmax is
 736                # just a constant offset, indistinguishable from A.  Penalise alpha by
 737                # exp(-|n_a|): coupling=1 at n=0, 0.37 at n=1, 0.14 at n=2.
 738                # This keeps alpha near 0 until the data pushes n_a away from 0.
 739                if use_alpha and alpha_n_coupling > 0.0:
 740                    _flatness_a = torch.exp(-torch.abs(n_a))  # [T] or [T, K-1]
 741                    if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 742                        pyro.factor("alpha_n_coupling_a", -(alpha * _flatness_a * alpha_n_coupling).sum(dim=-1))
 743                    else:
 744                        pyro.factor("alpha_n_coupling_a", -(alpha * _flatness_a * alpha_n_coupling))
 745
 746                # Scale for Vmax, K is multiplied by alpha
 747                #eff_Vmax_sigma = alpha * Vmaxa_sigma + epsilon_tensor
 748                #eff_Ka_sigma   = alpha * Ka_sigma    + epsilon_tensor
 749
 750                # UNIFIED Vmax and K priors (Log-Normal for all distributions)
 751                # K uses CV-based std (scale-invariant, works without guides)
 752                # Vmax uses raw variance (data-driven) for negbinom/normal/studentt
 753
 754                # K parameterization (UNIFIED for all distributions)
 755                # When NTC mean is known, center the prior there with ±5 log2FC coverage.
 756                # This ensures the P.O.I. starts within the observed x-range regardless of
 757                # whether the subset is KO-only, CA-only, or full.
 758                #
 759                # Minimum prior width: K_log_sigma >= 5*ln(2)/2 ≈ 1.73
 760                # This guarantees the lower end of the 95% CI extends at least 2^{-5} (1/32x)
 761                # below the prior centre, matching the NTC-centred branch below.
 762                _K_log_sigma_min = (k_log_sigma_min_tensor
 763                                    if k_log_sigma_min_tensor is not None
 764                                    else self._t(5.0 * 0.6931 / 2.0))
 765
 766                if x_ntc_mean is not None:
 767                    # K prior: log-normal with MEDIAN at x_ntc_mean (= log2FC 0).
 768                    # In log2FC space: log2(K_a) ~ Normal(0, sigma_log2²) where
 769                    # sigma_log2 = K_log_sigma / ln(2) = 2.5, giving a 95% CI of ±5 log2FC.
 770                    # Setting K_log_mu = log(x_ntc_mean) centres the median (not the mean)
 771                    # at NTC, which is the natural reference in log2FC space.
 772                    K_log_sigma = _K_log_sigma_min  # = 5*ln(2)/2 → sigma_log2 = 2.5
 773                    K_log_mu = torch.log(x_ntc_mean.clamp_min(epsilon_tensor))
 774                else:
 775                    # Fallback: centre median at user-specified quantile of x_true (k_prior_center).
 776                    # Default: middle of observed range (K_max/2). Width from CV.
 777                    # Floor sigma so the prior always spans at least ±5 log2FC.
 778                    _k_fallback = (k_center_tensor if k_center_tensor is not None
 779                                   else K_max_tensor / 2.0)
 780                    K_mean_prior = _k_fallback.clamp_min(epsilon_tensor)
 781                    if x_true_CV is not None:
 782                        K_std_prior = K_mean_prior * x_true_CV
 783                    else:
 784                        K_std_prior = K_max_tensor / (self._t(2.0) * torch.sqrt(K_alpha_tensor))
 785                    ratio_K = (K_std_prior / K_mean_prior).clamp_min(self._t(1e-6))
 786                    K_log_sigma = torch.sqrt(torch.log1p(ratio_K ** 2)).clamp_min(_K_log_sigma_min)
 787                    K_log_mu = torch.log(K_mean_prior)
 788
 789                if distribution in ['binomial', 'multinomial']:
 790                    # For binomial/multinomial: Sample Vmax_a INDEPENDENTLY (like BCD1C4F)
 791                    # Even for multinomial, the Kth category is residual, so we can have independent Vmax
 792                    # This gives Vmax_a direct gradient signal, not mediated through alpha
 793                    # Avoids chicken-and-egg: alpha needs signal → signal needs Vmax → Vmax needs alpha
 794                    Vmax_mean_clamped = Vmax_mean_tensor.clamp(min=0.01, max=0.99)
 795                    # concentration=2 gives CV ≈ 0.6-1.0 depending on the mean —
 796                    # much more diffuse than the previous 10, allowing the posterior
 797                    # to explore Vmax values well above the data-driven estimate when
 798                    # only part of the dose-response range is observed.
 799                    concentration_vmax = self._t(2.0)
 800                    alpha_vmax = Vmax_mean_clamped * concentration_vmax
 801                    beta_vmax = (1 - Vmax_mean_clamped) * concentration_vmax
 802
 803                    if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 804                        # For multinomial: Sample Vmax_a for K-1 categories (Kth is residual)
 805                        # Use .to_event(1) instead of nested plates to avoid dim=-1 collision with trans_plate
 806                        K_minus_1 = K - 1
 807                        Vmax_a = pyro.sample("Vmax_a", dist.Beta(alpha_vmax[:, :K_minus_1], beta_vmax[:, :K_minus_1]).to_event(1))  # [T, K-1]
 808
 809                        # K_a: Log-Normal for K-1 categories
 810                        log_K_a = pyro.sample("log_K_a", dist.Normal(K_log_mu, K_log_sigma).expand([K_minus_1]).to_event(1))  # [T, K-1]
 811                        K_a = pyro.deterministic("K_a", torch.exp(log_K_a))  # [T, K-1]
 812                    else:
 813                        # For binomial: per-feature Vmax_a and K_a
 814                        Vmax_a = pyro.sample("Vmax_a", dist.Beta(alpha_vmax, beta_vmax))  # [T]
 815                        log_K_a = pyro.sample("log_K_a", dist.Normal(K_log_mu, K_log_sigma))  # [T]
 816                        K_a = pyro.deterministic("K_a", torch.exp(log_K_a))  # [T]
 817
 818                else:
 819                    # Vmax prior: LogNormal for negbinom, normal, and studentt alike.
 820                    # Direction of effect is carried by n (negative n = repressor Hill),
 821                    # so Vmax must be strictly positive for all three distributions.
 822                    # Wide log_sigma (floor ≥ 1.5, ≈ 20× range) keeps the prior diffuse
 823                    # enough for one-sided subsets (single technical group).
 824                    _Vmax_log_sigma_floor = (vmax_log_sigma_floor_tensor
 825                                             if vmax_log_sigma_floor_tensor is not None
 826                                             else self._t(1.5))
 827                    Vmax_sigma = (Vmax_prior_mean / torch.sqrt(Vmax_alpha_tensor)) + epsilon_tensor
 828                    Vmax_log_sigma = torch.sqrt(
 829                        torch.log1p((Vmax_sigma / Vmax_prior_mean) ** 2)
 830                    ).clamp_min(_Vmax_log_sigma_floor)
 831                    Vmax_log_mu = (torch.log(Vmax_prior_mean.clamp_min(epsilon_tensor))
 832                                   - 0.5 * Vmax_log_sigma ** 2)
 833                    log_Vmax_a = pyro.sample("log_Vmax_a", dist.Normal(Vmax_log_mu, Vmax_log_sigma))
 834                    Vmax_a = pyro.deterministic("Vmax_a", torch.exp(log_Vmax_a))
 835
 836                    log_K_a = pyro.sample("log_K_a", dist.Normal(K_log_mu, K_log_sigma))
 837                    K_a = pyro.deterministic("K_a", torch.exp(log_K_a))
 838
 839                # Sample all required parameters (additive_hill and nested_hill need second set)
 840                if function_type in ['additive_hill', 'nested_hill']:
 841                    sigma_n_b = pyro.sample("sigma_n_b", dist.Exponential(self._t(1.0)))
 842                    if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 843                        # Use .to_event(1) instead of nested plate to avoid dim=-1 collision with trans_plate
 844                        beta = pyro.sample("beta", alpha_dist(temperature=temperature, logits=p_n_logits_tensor).expand([K - 1]).to_event(1))  # [T, K-1]
 845                    else:
 846                        beta = pyro.sample("beta", alpha_dist(temperature=temperature, logits=p_n_logits_tensor))  # [T]
 847
 848                    # n_b: per-category for multinomial, single for others
 849                    if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 850                        # Use .to_event(1) instead of nested plate to avoid dim=-1 collision with trans_plate
 851                        K_minus_1 = K - 1
 852                        n_b_raw = pyro.sample("n_b_raw", dist.Normal(n_mu_raw_tensor, sigma_n_b.unsqueeze(-1).expand(T, K_minus_1)).to_event(1))  # [T, K-1]
 853                        n_b = pyro.deterministic(
 854                            "n_b",
 855                            _soft_clamp(n_b_raw, nmin, nmax)
 856                        )  # [T, K-1]
 857                    else:
 858                        n_b_raw = pyro.sample("n_b_raw", dist.Normal(n_mu_raw_tensor, sigma_n_b))
 859                        n_b = pyro.deterministic(
 860                            "n_b",
 861                            _soft_clamp(n_b_raw, nmin, nmax)
 862                        )
 863
 864                    # Identifiability coupling for beta/n_b (same logic as alpha/n_a above).
 865                    if use_alpha and alpha_n_coupling > 0.0:
 866                        _flatness_b = torch.exp(-torch.abs(n_b))  # [T] or [T, K-1]
 867                        if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 868                            pyro.factor("alpha_n_coupling_b", -(beta * _flatness_b * alpha_n_coupling).sum(dim=-1))
 869                        else:
 870                            pyro.factor("alpha_n_coupling_b", -(beta * _flatness_b * alpha_n_coupling))
 871
 872                    # Vmax_b and K_b: same structure as Vmax_a and K_a
 873                    if distribution in ['binomial', 'multinomial']:
 874                        if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 875                            # For multinomial: Sample Vmax_b for K-1 categories (Kth is residual)
 876                            # Use .to_event(1) instead of nested plates to avoid dim=-1 collision with trans_plate
 877                            K_minus_1 = K - 1
 878                            Vmax_b = pyro.sample("Vmax_b", dist.Beta(alpha_vmax[:, :K_minus_1], beta_vmax[:, :K_minus_1]).to_event(1))  # [T, K-1]
 879
 880                            # K_b: Log-Normal for K-1 categories
 881                            log_K_b = pyro.sample("log_K_b", dist.Normal(K_log_mu, K_log_sigma).expand([K_minus_1]).to_event(1))  # [T, K-1]
 882                            K_b = pyro.deterministic("K_b", torch.exp(log_K_b))  # [T, K-1]
 883                        else:
 884                            # For binomial: per-feature Vmax_b and K_b
 885                            Vmax_b = pyro.sample("Vmax_b", dist.Beta(alpha_vmax, beta_vmax))  # [T]
 886                            log_K_b = pyro.sample("log_K_b", dist.Normal(K_log_mu, K_log_sigma))  # [T]
 887                            K_b = pyro.deterministic("K_b", torch.exp(log_K_b))  # [T]
 888
 889                    else:
 890                        # Vmax_b: same LogNormal prior as Vmax_a (parameters computed above).
 891                        log_Vmax_b = pyro.sample("log_Vmax_b", dist.Normal(Vmax_log_mu, Vmax_log_sigma))
 892                        Vmax_b = pyro.deterministic("Vmax_b", torch.exp(log_Vmax_b))
 893
 894                        log_K_b = pyro.sample("log_K_b", dist.Normal(K_log_mu, K_log_sigma))
 895                        K_b = pyro.deterministic("K_b", torch.exp(log_K_b))
 896                
 897                # Early exit for memory-efficient posterior sampling.
 898                # All gene-level latent variables (A, alpha, beta, Vmax_a/b, K_a/b, n_a/b,
 899                # o_y, sigma_n_a/b) have been sampled above as [T]-shaped tensors.
 900                # Skipping the cell-level Hill computation avoids creating [N, T] tensors
 901                # (each ~2.68 GB for N=29318, T=22834), which is the source of OOM during
 902                # pyro.infer.Predictive with num_samples > 1.
 903                if latents_only:
 904                    return
 905
 906                # Compute Hill function(s)
 907                # Hill_based_positive returns values in [0, Vmax]
 908                # We compute: y = A + alpha * Hill + beta * Hill (for additive)
 909
 910                if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 911                    # NEW FORMULATION for multinomial (matching binomial structure):
 912                    # Sample A from Dirichlet (sum to 1)
 913                    # Sample Vmax_a and Vmax_b INDEPENDENTLY for K-1 categories (Kth is residual)
 914                    # For each category k in K-1:
 915                    #   y_k = A_k + (alpha * Hill_a_k(Vmax=Vmax_a_k)) + (beta * Hill_b_k(Vmax=Vmax_b_k))
 916                    # Then: y_K = 1 - sum(y_1, ..., y_{K-1})
 917                    # This ensures probabilities sum to 1, and Kth category gets whatever is left
 918
 919                    K_dim = K
 920                    K_minus_1 = K - 1
 921                    # x_3d: [N, 1, 1] broadcasts over [1, T, K-1] parameter tensors
 922                    x_3d = x_true.unsqueeze(1).unsqueeze(2)  # [N, 1, 1]
 923
 924                    # A is [T, K] from Dirichlet
 925                    # Extract K-1 for fitting Hills (Kth doesn't get a Hill function)
 926                    A_kminus1 = A[..., :K_minus_1]  # [T, K-1]
 927
 928                    # Expand for broadcasting
 929                    A_kminus1_expanded = A_kminus1.unsqueeze(0)  # [1, T, K-1]
 930
 931                    if function_type == 'single_hill':
 932                        # Vectorized over K-1: Vmax_a/log_K_a/n_a all [T, K-1]
 933                        Hilla_kminus1 = Hill_based_positive_logK(
 934                            x_3d, Vmax=Vmax_a.unsqueeze(0), A=0,
 935                            logK=log_K_a.unsqueeze(0), n=n_a.unsqueeze(0)
 936                        )  # [N, T, K-1]
 937                        combined_hill = alpha.unsqueeze(0) * Hilla_kminus1  # [N, T, K-1]
 938                        y_kminus1 = A_kminus1_expanded + combined_hill      # [N, T, K-1]
 939
 940                    elif function_type == 'additive_hill':
 941                        # Vectorized over K-1 for both Hill_a and Hill_b
 942                        Hilla_kminus1 = Hill_based_positive_logK(
 943                            x_3d, Vmax=Vmax_a.unsqueeze(0), A=0,
 944                            logK=log_K_a.unsqueeze(0), n=n_a.unsqueeze(0)
 945                        )  # [N, T, K-1]
 946                        Hillb_kminus1 = Hill_based_positive_logK(
 947                            x_3d, Vmax=Vmax_b.unsqueeze(0), A=0,
 948                            logK=log_K_b.unsqueeze(0), n=n_b.unsqueeze(0)
 949                        )  # [N, T, K-1]
 950                        combined_hill = (alpha.unsqueeze(0) * Hilla_kminus1 +
 951                                         beta.unsqueeze(0) * Hillb_kminus1)  # [N, T, K-1]
 952                        y_kminus1 = A_kminus1_expanded + combined_hill         # [N, T, K-1]
 953
 954                    elif function_type == 'nested_hill':
 955                        # First Hill vectorized over K-1; its output feeds the second Hill
 956                        Hilla_kminus1 = Hill_based_positive_logK(
 957                            x_3d, Vmax=Vmax_a.unsqueeze(0), A=0,
 958                            logK=log_K_a.unsqueeze(0), n=n_a.unsqueeze(0)
 959                        )  # [N, T, K-1]
 960                        Hillb_kminus1 = Hill_based_positive(
 961                            Hilla_kminus1, Vmax=Vmax_b.unsqueeze(0), A=0,
 962                            K=K_b.unsqueeze(0), n=n_b.unsqueeze(0),
 963                            epsilon=epsilon_tensor
 964                        )  # [N, T, K-1]
 965                        combined_hill = alpha.unsqueeze(0) * Hillb_kminus1  # [N, T, K-1]
 966                        y_kminus1 = A_kminus1_expanded + combined_hill      # [N, T, K-1]
 967
 968                    # Clamp K-1 probabilities to [epsilon, 1-epsilon] to ensure valid residual
 969                    y_kminus1 = torch.clamp(y_kminus1, min=epsilon_tensor, max=1.0 - epsilon_tensor)
 970
 971                    # Ensure sum of K-1 doesn't exceed 1
 972                    sum_kminus1 = y_kminus1.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)  # [N, T, 1]
 973                    # If sum > (1-epsilon), rescale proportionally
 974                    y_kminus1 = torch.where(
 975                        sum_kminus1 > (1.0 - epsilon_tensor),
 976                        y_kminus1 * (1.0 - epsilon_tensor) / sum_kminus1,
 977                        y_kminus1
 978                    )
 979
 980                    # Compute Kth category as residual: y_K = 1 - sum(y_1, ..., y_{K-1})
 981                    y_K = 1.0 - y_kminus1.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)  # [N, T, 1]
 982                    y_K = torch.clamp(y_K, min=epsilon_tensor, max=1.0 - epsilon_tensor)
 983
 984                    # Concatenate to get all K probabilities
 985                    y_dose_response = torch.cat([y_kminus1, y_K], dim=-1)  # [N, T, K]
 986
 987                else:
 988                    # For non-multinomial: standard Hill computation
 989                    if distribution == 'binomial':
 990                        # For binomial: use log_K_a/log_K_b (numerically stable sigmoid formulation)
 991                        # y = A + (alpha * Hill_a(Vmax=Vmax_a)) + (beta * Hill_b(Vmax=Vmax_b))
 992                        # Note: Vmax_a + Vmax_b CAN exceed 1 - we'll try without clamp first
 993
 994                        if function_type == 'single_hill':
 995                            Hilla = Hill_based_positive_logK(x_true.unsqueeze(-1), Vmax=Vmax_a, A=0, logK=log_K_a, n=n_a)
 996                            y_dose_response = A + (alpha * Hilla)
 997
 998                        elif function_type == 'additive_hill':
 999                            Hilla = Hill_based_positive_logK(x_true.unsqueeze(-1), Vmax=Vmax_a, A=0, logK=log_K_a, n=n_a)
1000                            Hillb = Hill_based_positive_logK(x_true.unsqueeze(-1), Vmax=Vmax_b, A=0, logK=log_K_b, n=n_b)
1001                            y_dose_response = A + (alpha * Hilla) + (beta * Hillb)
1002
1003                        elif function_type == 'nested_hill':
1004                            Hilla = Hill_based_positive_logK(x_true.unsqueeze(-1), Vmax=Vmax_a, A=0, logK=log_K_a, n=n_a)
1005                            Hillb = Hill_based_positive(Hilla, Vmax=Vmax_b, A=0, K=K_b, n=n_b, epsilon=epsilon_tensor)
1006                            y_dose_response = A + (alpha * Hillb)
1007
1008                        # OPTIONAL CLAMP (commented out for now - try without first):
1009                        # If Vmax_a + Vmax_b > 1 causes issues, uncomment:
1010                        # y_dose_response = torch.clamp(y_dose_response, min=epsilon_tensor, max=1.0 - epsilon_tensor)
1011
1012                    else:
1013                        # For negbinom/normal/studentt: log_K_a/b are always available
1014                        # (log-normal prior is now the only path), so always use logK variant.
1015                        if function_type == 'single_hill':
1016                            Hilla = Hill_based_positive_logK(x_true.unsqueeze(-1), Vmax=Vmax_a, A=0, logK=log_K_a, n=n_a)
1017                            y_dose_response = A + (alpha * Hilla)
1018                        elif function_type == 'additive_hill':
1019                            Hilla = Hill_based_positive_logK(x_true.unsqueeze(-1), Vmax=Vmax_a, A=0, logK=log_K_a, n=n_a)
1020                            Hillb = Hill_based_positive_logK(x_true.unsqueeze(-1), Vmax=Vmax_b, A=0, logK=log_K_b, n=n_b)
1021                            y_dose_response = A + (alpha * Hilla) + (beta * Hillb)
1022                        elif function_type == 'nested_hill':
1023                            Hilla = Hill_based_positive_logK(x_true.unsqueeze(-1), Vmax=Vmax_a, A=0, logK=log_K_a, n=n_a)
1024                            Hillb = Hill_based_positive_logK(Hilla, Vmax=Vmax_b, A=0, logK=log_K_b, n=n_b)
1025                            y_dose_response = A + (alpha * Hillb)
1026
1027            elif function_type == 'polynomial':
1028                assert polynomial_degree is not None and polynomial_degree >= 1, \
1029                    "polynomial_degree must be ≥ 1 (no intercept, A is handled separately)"
1030
1031                if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
1032                    # For multinomial: fit K independent polynomials (one per category) in logit space
1033                    # Then apply softmax to get K probabilities that sum to 1
1034                    # This is more standard than K-1 with residual for unbounded logit space
1035
1036                    # Sample per-category polynomial coefficients
1037                    coeffs_per_category = []
1038                    for d in range(1, polynomial_degree + 1):
1039                        with pyro.plate(f"poly_category_plate_deg{d}", K, dim=-2):
1040                            coeff = pyro.sample(f"poly_coeff_{d}", dist.Normal(0., sigma_coeff))  # [K, T]
1041                            coeffs_per_category.append(coeff)
1042                    coeffs = torch.stack(coeffs_per_category, dim=-3)  # [degree, K, T]
1043
1044                    if latents_only:
1045                        return
1046
1047                    # Compute polynomial for each category
1048                    # coeffs: [degree, K, T]
1049                    # Need to permute to [degree, T, K] for Polynomial_function to work correctly
1050                    coeffs_permuted = coeffs.permute(0, 2, 1)  # [degree, T, K]
1051                    poly_val = Polynomial_function(x_true_sample, coeffs_permuted)  # [N, T, K]
1052
1053                    # A is baseline logit for each category (need K logits)
1054                    # Sample K baseline logits (unbounded)
1055                    with pyro.plate("category_plate_A", K, dim=-2):
1056                        A_clamped = torch.clamp(A.unsqueeze(-2), min=epsilon_tensor, max=1.0 - epsilon_tensor)  # [1, T]
1057                        logit_A_transpose = torch.log(A_clamped) - torch.log(1 - A_clamped)  # [K, T] logits
1058                    logit_A = logit_A_transpose.transpose(-1, -2)  # [T, K]
1059
1060                    # Compute logits for each category
1061                    logits_K = logit_A.unsqueeze(0) + alpha.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(-1) * poly_val  # [N, T, K]
1062
1063                    # Apply softmax to get probabilities that sum to 1
1064                    y_dose_response = torch.softmax(logits_K, dim=-1)  # [N, T, K]
1065
1066                else:
1067                    # For non-multinomial: single set of coefficients per feature
1068                    # Stack polynomial coefficients
1069                    coeffs = []
1070                    for d in range(1, polynomial_degree + 1):  # start at degree 1, no intercept
1071                        coeff = pyro.sample(f"poly_coeff_{d}", dist.Normal(0., sigma_coeff))
1072                        coeffs.append(coeff)
1073                    coeffs = torch.stack(coeffs, dim=-2)  # [degree, T]
1074                    if (coeffs.shape[1] == 1) & (coeffs.ndim == 4):
1075                        coeffs = coeffs.squeeze(1)        # [S, D, T]
1076
1077                    if latents_only:
1078                        return
1079
1080                    # Distribution-specific polynomial computation:
1081                    if distribution in ['normal', 'studentt']:
1082                        # For continuous distributions: work in natural space (no logs!)
1083                        # Polynomial is applied to x_true directly: y = A + alpha * poly(x)
1084                        poly_val = Polynomial_function(x_true_sample, coeffs)  # [N, T]
1085                        y_dose_response = A + alpha * poly_val  # [N, T] - can be negative!
1086
1087                    elif distribution in ['negbinom']:
1088                        # For negbinom: work in log space
1089                        # Polynomial is applied to log2(x): log2(y) = log2(A) + alpha * poly(log2(x))
1090                        log2_x_true = torch.log2(x_true_sample)  # [N]
1091                        poly_val = Polynomial_function(log2_x_true, coeffs)  # [N, T]
1092                        log2_y_dose_response = torch.log2(A) + alpha * poly_val  # [N, T]
1093                        y_dose_response = 2 ** log2_y_dose_response  # Convert back to count space
1094
1095                    elif distribution == 'binomial':
1096                        # For binomial: work in LOGIT space (unbounded: -inf to +inf)
1097                        # A is in [0,1] from Beta prior, convert to logit
1098                        # Polynomial is applied to x_true: logit(p) = logit(A) + alpha * poly(x)
1099                        A_clamped = torch.clamp(A, min=epsilon_tensor, max=1.0 - epsilon_tensor)
1100                        logit_A = torch.log(A_clamped) - torch.log(1 - A_clamped)  # logit(A)
1101                        poly_val = Polynomial_function(x_true_sample, coeffs)  # [N, T]
1102                        logit_p = logit_A + alpha * poly_val  # [N, T] - logit space (unbounded)
1103                        # Convert back to probability space for sampler
1104                        y_dose_response = torch.sigmoid(logit_p)  # [N, T] in [0, 1]
1105
1106                    else:
1107                        raise ValueError(f"Unknown distribution for polynomial: {distribution}")
1108            else:
1109                raise ValueError(f"Unknown function_type: {function_type}")
1110            
1111
1112        ##########################
1113        ## Cell-level variables ##
1114        ##########################
1115        # At this point, y_dose_response contains the dose-response function output.
1116        # We need to transform it to the format expected by samplers.
1117        #
1118        # IMPORTANT: Samplers in distributions.py handle technical group effects themselves!
1119        # Do NOT apply alpha_y here - pass it to the sampler via alpha_y_full.
1120
1121        # Prepare alpha_y_full (full C technical groups, including reference)
1122        # This will be passed to samplers, which apply technical groups themselves
1123        # Multinomial now supported (additive on logit scale, like binomial)
1124        if alpha_y is not None and groups_tensor is not None:
1125            # CRITICAL: Check if alpha_y already includes reference group
1126            # If alpha_y.shape[0 or 1] == C, it already has reference, don't add it!
1127
1128            if alpha_y.dim() == 4:  # Predictive multinomial: Could be (S, C-1, T, K) or (S, C, T, K)
1129                if alpha_y.shape[1] == C:
1130                    # Already includes reference
1131                    alpha_y_full = alpha_y
1132                else:
1133                    # Need to add reference (zeros for additive on logit scale)
1134                    baseline_shape = (alpha_y.shape[0], 1, alpha_y.shape[2], alpha_y.shape[3])
1135                    baseline = torch.zeros(baseline_shape, device=self.model.device)
1136                    alpha_y_full = torch.cat([baseline, alpha_y], dim=1)
1137
1138            elif alpha_y.dim() == 3:
1139                # Could be Predictive 2D (S, C-1, T) or Training multinomial (C-1, T, K) or (C, T, K)
1140                # Check if last dimension matches K (multinomial) or T (2D predictive)
1141                if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None and alpha_y.shape[-1] == K:
1142                    # Training multinomial: (C-1, T, K) or (C, T, K)
1143                    if alpha_y.shape[0] == C:
1144                        # Already includes reference
1145                        alpha_y_full = alpha_y
1146                    else:
1147                        # Need to add reference (zeros for additive on logit scale)
1148                        baseline_shape = (1, alpha_y.shape[1], alpha_y.shape[2])
1149                        baseline = torch.zeros(baseline_shape, device=self.model.device)
1150                        alpha_y_full = torch.cat([baseline, alpha_y], dim=0)
1151                else:
1152                    # Predictive 2D: (S, C-1, T) or (S, C, T)
1153                    if alpha_y.shape[1] == C:
1154                        # Already includes reference
1155                        alpha_y_full = alpha_y
1156                    else:
1157                        # Need to add reference (zeros for additive, ones for multiplicative)
1158                        ones_shape = (alpha_y.shape[0], 1, T)
1159                        if distribution == 'negbinom':
1160                            baseline = torch.ones(ones_shape, device=self.model.device)
1161                        else:
1162                            baseline = torch.zeros(ones_shape, device=self.model.device)
1163                        alpha_y_full = torch.cat([baseline, alpha_y], dim=1)
1164
1165            elif alpha_y.dim() == 2:  # Training 2D: Could be (C-1, T) or (C, T)
1166                if alpha_y.shape[0] == C:
1167                    # Already includes reference
1168                    alpha_y_full = alpha_y
1169                else:
1170                    # Need to add reference (zeros for additive, ones for multiplicative)
1171                    ones_shape = (1, T)
1172                    if distribution == 'negbinom':
1173                        baseline = torch.ones(ones_shape, device=self.model.device)
1174                    else:
1175                        baseline = torch.zeros(ones_shape, device=self.model.device)
1176                    alpha_y_full = torch.cat([baseline, alpha_y], dim=0)
1177            else:
1178                raise ValueError(f"Unexpected alpha_y shape: {alpha_y.shape}")
1179        else:
1180            alpha_y_full = None
1181
1182        # Transform dose-response to sampler-expected format
1183        # (samplers will handle technical groups and normalization)
1184        if distribution == 'negbinom':
1185            # Sampler expects: mu_y = dose-response in count space (NO technical groups, NO sum factors)
1186            # Sampler will apply: mu_final = mu_y * alpha_y * sum_factor
1187            mu_y = y_dose_response  # [N, T] - just the dose-response
1188
1189        elif distribution == 'binomial':
1190            # Sampler expects: mu_y = probability in [0, 1]
1191            # y_dose_response should already be a probability from Hill/polynomial
1192            # Sampler will apply technical groups on logit scale
1193            mu_y = y_dose_response  # [N, T] - already probability
1194
1195        elif distribution == 'multinomial':
1196            # Sampler expects: mu_y = baseline probabilities [N, T, K]
1197            # y_dose_response is already [N, T, K] probabilities that sum to 1
1198            # Sampler will apply technical groups on logit scale per category
1199            # Zero out phantom categories so _masked_softmax in sample_multinomial_trans
1200            # correctly excludes them (it detects masked positions via mu_y == 0).
1201            obs_total = y_obs_tensor.sum(dim=0, keepdim=True)  # [1, T, K]
1202            mu_y = y_dose_response.masked_fill(obs_total == 0, 0.0)  # [N, T, K]
1203
1204        elif distribution in ['normal', 'studentt']:
1205            # Sampler expects: mu_y = natural value space
1206            # Sampler will apply technical groups additively
1207            mu_y = y_dose_response  # [N, T] - can be negative!
1208
1209        else:
1210            raise ValueError(f"Unknown distribution: {distribution}")
1211
1212        # Debug checks (keep for troubleshooting)
1213        if torch.isnan(mu_y).any() or torch.isinf(mu_y).any():
1214            check_tensor("mu_y", mu_y)
1215            check_tensor("y_dose_response", y_dose_response)
1216            check_tensor("sum_factor_tensor", sum_factor_tensor)
1217            check_tensor("phi_y_used", phi_y_used)
1218            check_tensor("A", A)
1219            if function_type in ['single_hill', 'additive_hill', 'nested_hill']:
1220                check_tensor("n_a", n_a)
1221                check_tensor("Vmax_a", Vmax_a)
1222                check_tensor("K_a", K_a)
1223            if function_type in ['additive_hill', 'nested_hill']:
1224                check_tensor("n_b", n_b)
1225                check_tensor("Vmax_b", Vmax_b)
1226                check_tensor("K_b", K_b)
1227            if function_type == 'polynomial':
1228                check_tensor("coeffs", coeffs)
1229
1230        # Call distribution-specific observation sampler
1231        from .distributions import get_observation_sampler
1232        observation_sampler = get_observation_sampler(distribution, 'trans')
1233
1234        # Call the appropriate sampler based on distribution
1235        if distribution == 'negbinom':
1236            observation_sampler(
1237                y_obs_tensor=y_obs_tensor,
1238                mu_y=mu_y,
1239                phi_y_used=phi_y_used,
1240                alpha_y_full=alpha_y_full,
1241                groups_tensor=groups_tensor,
1242                sum_factor_tensor=sum_factor_tensor,
1243                N=N,
1244                T=T,
1245                C=C,
1246                use_epsilon=use_epsilon
1247            )
1248        elif distribution == 'multinomial':
1249            # For multinomial, mu_y should be probabilities [N, T, K]
1250            observation_sampler(
1251                y_obs_tensor=y_obs_tensor,
1252                mu_y=mu_y,  # Should be [N, T, K] probabilities
1253                alpha_y_full=alpha_y_full,  # [C, T, K] or [S, C, T, K] - additive on logit scale
1254                groups_tensor=groups_tensor,
1255                N=N,
1256                T=T,
1257                K=K,
1258                C=C
1259            )
1260        elif distribution == 'binomial':
1261            observation_sampler(
1262                y_obs_tensor=y_obs_tensor,
1263                denominator_tensor=denominator_tensor,
1264                mu_y=mu_y,  # Should be probabilities [N, T]
1265                alpha_y_full=alpha_y_full,
1266                groups_tensor=groups_tensor,
1267                N=N,
1268                T=T,
1269                C=C
1270            )
1271        elif distribution == 'normal':
1272            observation_sampler(
1273                y_obs_tensor=y_obs_tensor,
1274                mu_y=mu_y,
1275                sigma_y=sigma_y,
1276                alpha_y_full=alpha_y_full,
1277                groups_tensor=groups_tensor,
1278                N=N,
1279                T=T,
1280                C=C
1281            )
1282        elif distribution == 'studentt':
1283            observation_sampler(
1284                y_obs_tensor=y_obs_tensor,
1285                mu_y=mu_y,
1286                sigma_y=sigma_y,
1287                nu_y=nu_y,
1288                alpha_y_full=alpha_y_full,
1289                groups_tensor=groups_tensor,
1290                N=N,
1291                T=T,
1292                C=C
1293            )
1294        else:
1295            raise ValueError(f"Unknown distribution: {distribution}")
1296
1297    ########################################################
1298    # Step 3: Fit trans effects (model_y)
1299    ########################################################
1300    def fit_trans(
1301        self,
1302        sum_factor_col: str = None,
1303        function_type: str = 'single_hill',  # or 'additive', 'nested'
1304        polynomial_degree: int = 6,
1305        lr: float = None,
1306        niters: int = None,
1307        nsamples: int = 1000,
1308        alpha_ewma: float = 0.05,
1309        beta_o_beta: float = 3, # recommended to keep based on cell2location
1310        beta_o_alpha: float = 9, # recommended to keep based on cell2location
1311        K_alpha: float = 2,
1312        Vmax_alpha: float = 2,
1313        n_mu: float = 0,
1314        p_n: float = 1e-6,
1315        epsilon: float = 1e-6,
1316        init_temp: float = 1.0,
1317        #final_temp: float = 1e-8,
1318        final_temp: float = 0.1,
1319        minibatch_size: int = None,
1320        distribution: str = None,
1321        denominator: np.ndarray = None,
1322        modality_name: str = None,
1323        min_denominator: int = None,
1324        use_epsilon: bool = False,
1325        warmup: bool = True,
1326        warmup_T_min: float = 0.5,
1327        vmax_log_sigma_floor: float = 1.5,
1328        k_log_sigma_min: float = None,
1329        k_prior_center: str = 'middle',
1330        checkpoint_interval: int = 10_000,
1331        checkpoint_dir: str = None,
1332        predictive_checkpoint: str = None,
1333        restart_from_checkpoint: bool = True,
1334        alpha_n_coupling: float = 10.0,
1335        debug: bool = False,
1336        **kwargs
1337    ):
1338        """
1339        Fit trans effects using distribution-specific likelihood.
1340
1341        Parameters
1342        ----------
1343        modality_name : str, optional
1344            Name of modality to fit. If None, uses primary modality.
1345        distribution : str, optional
1346            Distribution type: 'negbinom', 'multinomial', 'binomial', 'normal'
1347            If None, auto-detected from modality.
1348        sum_factor_col : str, optional
1349            Sum factor column name. Required for negbinom, ignored for others.
1350        denominator : np.ndarray, optional
1351            Denominator array for binomial distribution (e.g., total counts for PSI)
1352            If None, auto-detected from modality.
1353        min_denominator : int, optional
1354            Minimum denominator value for binomial observations. Observations where
1355            denominator < min_denominator are masked (excluded from fitting).
1356            Useful for filtering low-coverage splicing junctions. Default: None (no filtering).
1357        use_epsilon : bool, optional
1358            If True, add 1e-8 epsilon for numerical stability in NegativeBinomial logits.
1359            If False (default), use log(mu) - log(phi) directly.
1360        warmup : bool, optional
1361            For additive_hill/nested_hill: run a single_hill warmup phase before the main
1362            fit. Default True (warmup is on by default for additive/nested hill).
1363            Ignored for single_hill and polynomial.
1364        warmup_T_min : float, optional
1365            Temperature at which Phase 1 (single_hill warmup) ends. Phase 1 cools from
1366            init_temp down to warmup_T_min at the same rate as Phase 2, so the number of
1367            warmup steps is computed automatically:
1368                warmup_steps = round(niters * (init_temp - warmup_T_min) /
1369                                               (init_temp - final_temp))
1370            niters always refers to Phase 2 (additive_hill) steps; total steps =
1371            warmup_steps + niters. Default 0.5 (roughly half the annealing range,
1372            saves ~44% of a full single_hill run while still reaching the separation
1373            point where active and null genes are clearly distinguished).
1374        vmax_log_sigma_floor : float, optional
1375            Minimum log-sigma for the Vmax LogNormal prior (negbinom only).
1376            The data-driven log-sigma (≈ sqrt(log(1 + 1/Vmax_alpha))) is typically
1377            ≈0.65 and is always below this floor, so this parameter directly controls
1378            prior width. Default 1.5 (95% CI spans ≈exp(±3) ≈ 20× range).
1379            Previous default was 1.0 (7× range). Increase to allow Vmax to range
1380            more freely; set to 1.0 to restore the old behavior.
1381        k_log_sigma_min : float, optional
1382            Minimum log-sigma for the K LogNormal prior. Default None, which uses
1383            5*ln(2)/2 ≈ 1.733 (±5 log2FC = 32× range). Increase sparingly — K is
1384            already very wide, and wider K worsens the EC50 drift problem for genes
1385            where the Hill hasn't saturated within the observed x-range.
1386        k_prior_center : str, optional
1387            Where to centre the K (EC50) LogNormal prior when NTC cells are absent.
1388            Has no effect when NTC cells are present (prior is always centred at the
1389            NTC mean). Options:
1390            - 'lower'  : 5th percentile of x_true guide means. Use when the EC50 is
1391                         expected near baseline (e.g. strong activators where
1392                         half-maximum is reached at low cis expression).
1393            - 'middle' : half the maximum observed x_true (default, current behaviour).
1394            - 'upper'  : 95th percentile of x_true guide means. Use when the EC50 is
1395                         expected near the top of the observed range (e.g. repressors
1396                         where the effect only kicks in at high cis expression).
1397        predictive_checkpoint : str, optional
1398            Path to a checkpoint file to use for Predictive sampling only.  When set,
1399            all prior-computation setup runs as normal (same arguments as the original
1400            fit_trans call), but the training loop is skipped and the param_store is
