1401            loaded from the checkpoint instead.  Use this to draw posterior samples
1402            from any intermediate checkpoint without re-running training.
1403
1404            **function_type is auto-detected**: every checkpoint stores
1405            ``effective_function_type`` — the function that was *actually being
1406            fitted* when that checkpoint was written (``'single_hill'`` during
1407            warmup, the target type afterwards).  ``fit_trans`` reads this value
1408            before initialising the guide, so the guide architecture always matches
1409            the checkpoint.  ``warmup`` is also forced to ``False`` automatically.
1410            You therefore only need to pass ``sum_factor_col`` (and any other
1411            data-access arguments from the original call)::
1412
1413                model.fit_trans(
1414                    sum_factor_col='sum_factor_adj',
1415                    predictive_checkpoint='outdir/label/trans_checkpoint_gene_warmup.pt',
1416                )
1417
1418            The same minimal call works for any checkpoint — mid-warmup, post-warmup,
1419            or complete.
1420
1421            To inspect a checkpoint manually::
1422
1423                import torch
1424                ckpt = torch.load('trans_checkpoint_gene_step0030000.pt',
1425                                  map_location='cpu', weights_only=False)
1426                # Was this step in warmup?
1427                print(ckpt['effective_function_type'])  # 'single_hill' → yes, 'additive_hill' → no
1428                print(ckpt['phase2_announced'])         # False → in warmup, True → past it
1429
1430            Structural mismatches (N, T, K, C) raise an error; ``distribution``
1431            mismatches produce a warning.
1432        function_type : str
1433            Dose-response function: 'single_hill', 'additive_hill', 'polynomial'
1434        debug : bool, optional
1435            If True, run the slow debug SVI step that checks all parameters for
1436            non-finite values at every iteration and prints detailed diagnostics
1437            when NaN/Inf are detected. Default False (uses fast svi.step path).
1438            Enable when chasing NaN gradients or divergent parameters.
1439        **kwargs
1440            Additional parameters for specific distributions
1441
1442        Notes
1443        -----
1444        Each modality stores its own fitting results.
1445        Primary modality results are also stored at model level as ``model.posterior_samples_trans``.
1446        Trans fitting requires that technical fit has been performed for the modality.
1447
1448        If technical_group_code is set (via set_technical_groups()), it will be used for
1449        correction. Otherwise, no group correction is applied.
1450
1451        Examples
1452        --------
1453        >>> model.set_technical_groups(['cell_line'])  # Optional, for correction
1454        >>> model.fit_trans(sum_factor_col='sum_factor', function_type='additive_hill')
1455        """
1456
1457        if self.model.x_true is None:
1458            warnings.warn(
1459                "x_true not set. You should run fit_cis() before fit_trans(). "
1460                "Proceeding without cis effects."
1461            )
1462
1463        # Determine which modality to use
1464        if modality_name is None:
1465            modality_name = self.model.primary_modality
1466        modality = self.model.get_modality(modality_name)
1467
1468        # Auto-detect distribution from modality
1469        if distribution is None:
1470            distribution = modality.distribution
1471
1472        # Auto-detect denominator from modality (for binomial)
1473        if denominator is None and modality.denominator is not None:
1474            denominator = modality.denominator
1475
1476        # ---------------------------
1477        # Set conditional default for niters
1478        # ---------------------------
1479        if niters is None:
1480            # Default: 100,000 unless multinomial OR polynomial function, then 200,000
1481            # niters always means Phase 2 (additive/nested hill) steps.
1482            if distribution == 'multinomial':
1483                niters = 200_000
1484                if predictive_checkpoint is None:
1485                    print(f"[INFO] Using default niters=200,000 for multivariate distribution '{distribution}'")
1486            elif function_type == 'polynomial':
1487                niters = 200_000
1488                if predictive_checkpoint is None:
1489                    print(f"[INFO] Using default niters=200,000 for polynomial function")
1490            else:
1491                niters = 100_000
1492                if predictive_checkpoint is None:
1493                    print(f"[INFO] Using default niters=100,000 for distribution '{distribution}' and function_type '{function_type}'")
1494
1495        # ---------------------------
1496        # When predictive_checkpoint is given, read function_type directly from
1497        # the checkpoint's effective_function_type so the caller doesn't have to
1498        # specify it.  This must happen before _do_warmup and guide initialisation,
1499        # both of which depend on function_type.
1500        # ---------------------------
1501        if predictive_checkpoint is not None:
1502            try:
1503                _peek = torch.load(predictive_checkpoint, map_location='cpu', weights_only=False)
1504                _peek_ft = _peek.get('effective_function_type', _peek.get('function_type'))
1505                if _peek_ft is not None:
1506                    if _peek_ft != function_type:
1507                        print(f"[INFO] predictive_checkpoint: overriding "
1508                              f"function_type={function_type!r} → {_peek_ft!r} "
1509                              f"(read from checkpoint)")
1510                    function_type = _peek_ft
1511                # Suppress warmup — there's nothing to warm up when loading from a checkpoint
1512                warmup = False
1513            except Exception as e:
1514                warnings.warn(
1515                    f"Could not peek at predictive_checkpoint for function_type: {e}. "
1516                    f"Using caller-provided function_type={function_type!r}."
1517                )
1518
1519        # ---------------------------
1520        # Curriculum warmup: compute warmup_steps so Phase 1 cools at the same
1521        # rate as Phase 2 but stops at warmup_T_min instead of final_temp.
1522        # niters always refers to Phase 2 steps; total = warmup_steps + niters.
1523        # ---------------------------
1524        _do_warmup = (warmup and function_type in ['additive_hill', 'nested_hill'])
1525        if _do_warmup:
1526            if warmup_T_min >= init_temp:
1527                raise ValueError(
1528                    f"warmup_T_min ({warmup_T_min}) must be less than init_temp ({init_temp})"
1529                )
1530            if warmup_T_min < final_temp:
1531                import warnings as _w
1532                _w.warn(
1533                    f"warmup_T_min ({warmup_T_min}) is below final_temp ({final_temp}); "
1534                    f"Phase 1 will cool past the Phase 2 endpoint."
1535                )
1536            # Same cooling rate per step as Phase 2
1537            warmup_steps = round(niters * (init_temp - warmup_T_min) /
1538                                 (init_temp - final_temp))
1539            total_steps = warmup_steps + niters
1540            print(
1541                f"[INFO] Curriculum warmup: {warmup_steps} steps as single_hill "
1542                f"(T: {init_temp} → {warmup_T_min}), then {niters} steps as "
1543                f"{function_type} (T: {init_temp} → {final_temp}). "
1544                f"Total: {total_steps} steps."
1545            )
1546        else:
1547            warmup_steps = 0
1548            total_steps = niters
1549        
1550        if (modality.alpha_y_prefit is None
1551                and 'technical_group_code' in self.model.meta.columns):
1552            raise ValueError(
1553                f"Modality '{modality_name}' has not been fit with fit_ntc(). "
1554                f"Please run fit_ntc(modality_name='{modality_name}') first."
1555            )
1556
1557        # Get counts from modality (densify if sparse)
1558        counts_to_fit = modality.counts
1559        if hasattr(counts_to_fit, 'toarray'):
1560            counts_to_fit = counts_to_fit.toarray()
1561
1562        # Get cell names from modality
1563        if modality.cell_names is not None:
1564            modality_cells = modality.cell_names
1565        else:
1566            # Modality doesn't have cell names - assume same order as model.meta['cell']
1567            modality_cells = self.model.meta['cell'].values[:counts_to_fit.shape[modality.cells_axis]]
1568
1569        # Get technical fit results from modality (NOT self.model.alpha_y_prefit!)
1570        # DEFENSIVE: Use distribution-specific attributes first (like plot_xy_data does)
1571        # This is more robust than the generic alpha_y_prefit
1572        alpha_y_prefit = None
1573
1574        if distribution == 'negbinom':
1575            if hasattr(modality, 'alpha_y_prefit_mult') and modality.alpha_y_prefit_mult is not None:
1576                alpha_y_prefit = modality.alpha_y_prefit_mult
1577                print(f"[INFO] Using distribution-specific alpha_y_prefit_mult for {distribution}")
1578        else:
1579            if hasattr(modality, 'alpha_y_prefit_add') and modality.alpha_y_prefit_add is not None:
1580                alpha_y_prefit = modality.alpha_y_prefit_add
1581                print(f"[INFO] Using distribution-specific alpha_y_prefit_add for {distribution}")
1582
1583        # Fallback to generic attribute if distribution-specific not available
1584        if alpha_y_prefit is None and hasattr(modality, 'alpha_y_prefit') and modality.alpha_y_prefit is not None:
1585            alpha_y_prefit = modality.alpha_y_prefit
1586            print(f"[WARNING] Distribution-specific alpha_y not found, falling back to generic alpha_y_prefit. "
1587                  f"This may be incorrect if using old technical fit results. "
1588                  f"Consider re-running fit_ntc with current code.")
1589
1590        print(f"[INFO] Fitting trans model for modality '{modality_name}' (distribution: {distribution})")
1591
1592        # Validate min_denominator is specified for binomial/multinomial
1593        if distribution in ['binomial', 'multinomial'] and min_denominator is None:
1594            raise ValueError(
1595                f"min_denominator is required for distribution='{distribution}'. "
1596                f"Please specify min_denominator (e.g., min_denominator=0 for no filtering, "
1597                f"or min_denominator=3 for standard quality filtering)."
1598            )
1599
1600        # Validate distribution-specific requirements
1601        from .distributions import requires_sum_factor, requires_denominator
1602
1603        if requires_sum_factor(distribution) and sum_factor_col is None:
1604            raise ValueError(f"Distribution '{distribution}' requires sum_factor_col parameter")
1605
1606        if requires_sum_factor(distribution) and modality.sum_factors is None:
1607            raise ValueError(
1608                f"Modality '{modality_name}' has distribution '{distribution}' but no sum_factors "
1609                f"DataFrame has been set. Assign a cell-indexed DataFrame to "
1610                f"modality.sum_factors before calling fit_trans()."
1611            )
1612
1613        if requires_denominator(distribution) and denominator is None:
1614            raise ValueError(f"Distribution '{distribution}' requires denominator parameter")
1615
1616        # convert to gpu for fitting if applicable
1617        if self.model.x_true is not None and self.model.x_true.device != self.model.device:
1618            self.model.x_true = self.model.x_true.to(self.model.device)
1619        if alpha_y_prefit is not None and alpha_y_prefit.device != self.model.device:
1620            alpha_y_prefit = alpha_y_prefit.to(self.model.device)
1621
1622        if not hasattr(self.model, "log2_x_true") or self.model.log2_x_true is None:
1623            if self.model.x_true is not None:
1624                self.model.log2_x_true = torch.log2(self.model.x_true)
1625
1626        # Handle cell subsetting
1627        # CRITICAL: Preserve exact modality cell order when subsetting meta
1628        # Use .set_index().loc[] to ensure meta_subset has same order as modality_cells
1629        meta_with_index = self.model.meta.set_index('cell')
1630        meta_subset = meta_with_index.loc[modality_cells].reset_index()
1631
1632        # Verify we got all cells (debugging)
1633        if len(meta_subset) != len(modality_cells):
1634            missing = set(modality_cells) - set(meta_subset['cell'].values)
1635            raise ValueError(f"Some modality cells not found in meta: {missing}")
1636
1637        # Check if technical_group_code exists (for correction)
1638        if "technical_group_code" in meta_subset.columns:
1639            C = meta_subset['technical_group_code'].nunique()
1640            groups_tensor = torch.tensor(meta_subset['technical_group_code'].values, dtype=torch.long, device=self.model.device)
1641            print(f"[INFO] Using technical_group_code with {C} groups for correction")
1642        else:
1643            C = None
1644            groups_tensor = None
1645            if alpha_y_prefit is None:
1646                warnings.warn("no alpha_y_prefit and no technical_group_code, assuming no confounding effect.")
1647
1648        # Compute x_true subset for this modality's cells.
1649        # Modalities may cover a strict subset of model cells; we index x_true
1650        # by position in self.model.meta so the N-length x_true_subset aligns
1651        # exactly with the N-length y_obs.
1652        _all_model_cells = self.model.meta['cell'].tolist()
1653        _cell_index_map = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(_all_model_cells)}
1654        _cell_indices = [_cell_index_map[c] for c in modality_cells]
1655        _cell_idx_tensor = torch.tensor(_cell_indices, dtype=torch.long, device=self.model.device)
1656        x_true_subset = self.model.x_true[_cell_idx_tensor]
1657
1658        N = len(modality_cells)
1659
1660        # Modality counts are already in correct order matching modality_cells
1661        # Handle both 2D and 3D arrays
1662        if counts_to_fit.ndim == 2:
1663            if modality.cells_axis == 1:
1664                y_obs = counts_to_fit.T  # [T, N] -> [N, T]
1665            else:
1666                y_obs = counts_to_fit  # Already [N, T]
1667            T = y_obs.shape[1]
1668        elif counts_to_fit.ndim == 3:
1669            # 3D data: (features, cells, categories/dimensions)
1670            # Transpose to (cells, features, categories/dimensions)
1671            y_obs = counts_to_fit.transpose(1, 0, 2)  # [T, N, K] -> [N, T, K]
1672            T = counts_to_fit.shape[0]
1673        else:
1674            raise ValueError(f"Unexpected number of dimensions: {counts_to_fit.ndim}")
1675
1676        # Handle sum factors for modality cells
1677        if sum_factor_col is not None:
1678            sum_factor_vals = modality.sum_factors.loc[meta_subset['cell'].values, sum_factor_col].values
1679            # Guard: zero, NaN, or inf sum factors will produce -inf/NaN logits in the likelihood
1680            # (log(0) = -inf → NaN gradients for all features of that cell).
1681            n_zero = int((sum_factor_vals == 0).sum())
1682            n_nonfinite = int(~np.isfinite(sum_factor_vals).sum())
1683            if n_nonfinite > 0:
1684                raise ValueError(
1685                    f"[fit_trans] Column '{sum_factor_col}' has {n_nonfinite} non-finite (NaN/inf) value(s). "
1686                    f"Please fix before fitting."
1687                )
1688            if n_zero > 0:
1689                raise ValueError(
1690                    f"[fit_trans] Column '{sum_factor_col}' has {n_zero} zero value(s). "
1691                    f"Zero sum factors produce log(0)=-inf logits and NaN gradients for all features. "
1692                    f"If using sum_factor_refit, re-run refit_sumfactor() — it now floors values above zero."
1693                )
1694            sum_factor_tensor = torch.tensor(
1695                sum_factor_vals,
1696                dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device
1697            )
1698        else:
1699            sum_factor_tensor = torch.ones(N, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1700
1701        # Handle denominator for modality cells
1702        denominator_tensor = None
1703        if denominator is not None:
1704            if denominator.ndim == 2:
1705                if modality.cells_axis == 1:
1706                    denominator_subset = denominator.T  # [T, N] -> [N, T]
1707                else:
1708                    denominator_subset = denominator  # Already [N, T]
1709                denominator_tensor = torch.tensor(denominator_subset, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1710            elif denominator.ndim == 3:
1711                # 3D denominator (shouldn't happen for current distributions, but handle it)
1712                denominator_subset = denominator.transpose(1, 0, 2)
1713                denominator_tensor = torch.tensor(denominator_subset, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1714
1715            # Apply min_denominator filter if specified
1716            if min_denominator is not None and min_denominator > 0:
1717                # Create mask for observations where denominator < threshold
1718                low_coverage_mask = denominator_tensor < min_denominator
1719                n_masked = low_coverage_mask.sum().item()
1720                n_total = denominator_tensor.numel()
1721                pct_masked = 100 * n_masked / n_total if n_total > 0 else 0
1722
1723                print(f"[INFO] Filtering observations with denominator < {min_denominator}")
1724                print(f"[INFO] Masked {n_masked}/{n_total} observations ({pct_masked:.1f}%)")
1725
1726                # For binomial distributions, we'll pass the mask to the model
1727                # The sampler will need to handle it (for now, set those observations to special value)
1728                # We'll use a very negative value that the sampler can detect
1729                # Actually, better approach: modify y_obs to have NaN for masked observations
1730                # But binomial doesn't support NaN observations...
1731                # Best approach: set denominator=0 for masked observations, and sampler handles it
1732                denominator_tensor = torch.where(low_coverage_mask,
1733                                                 torch.zeros_like(denominator_tensor),
1734                                                 denominator_tensor)
1735
1736        # Detect data dimensions (for multinomial)
1737        from .distributions import is_3d_distribution
1738        K = None
1739        if is_3d_distribution(distribution):
1740            if y_obs.ndim == 3:
1741                if distribution == 'multinomial':
1742                    K = y_obs.shape[2]  # Number of categories
1743            else:
1744                raise ValueError(f"Distribution '{distribution}' requires 3D data but got shape {y_obs.shape}")
1745        x_true_mean = x_true_subset
1746        beta_o_alpha_tensor = torch.tensor(beta_o_alpha, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1747        beta_o_beta_tensor = torch.tensor(beta_o_beta, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1748        K_alpha_tensor = torch.tensor(K_alpha, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1749        Vmax_alpha_tensor = torch.tensor(Vmax_alpha, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1750        n_mu_tensor = torch.tensor(n_mu, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1751        _k_log_sigma_min_val = k_log_sigma_min if k_log_sigma_min is not None else 5.0 * 0.6931 / 2.0
1752        vmax_log_sigma_floor_tensor = torch.tensor(vmax_log_sigma_floor, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1753        k_log_sigma_min_tensor = torch.tensor(_k_log_sigma_min_val, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1754        y_obs_tensor = torch.tensor(y_obs, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1755        epsilon_tensor = torch.tensor(epsilon, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1756        p_n_tensor = torch.tensor(p_n, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1757        # Pre-compute logits for RelaxedBernoulli (more numerically stable than probs)
1758        # logits = log(p / (1-p))
1759        p_n_logits_tensor = torch.tensor(np.log(p_n / (1 - p_n)), dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1760
1761        # --- robust, finite bounds for n to avoid overflow in x**n ---
1762        # use the same x_true sample type you use elsewhere
1763        x_for_bounds = x_true_subset
1764        x_min = torch.clamp(x_for_bounds.min(), min=1e-12)  # strictly > 0 to avoid log(0)
1765        x_max = x_for_bounds.max()
1766
1767        log_fmax = torch.log(torch.tensor(torch.finfo(torch.float32).max, device=self.model.device))
1768
1769        # candidates can be inf if denominator ~ 0; we cap them later
1770        nmin_cand = (-log_fmax / torch.abs(torch.log(x_min))) if (x_min < 1) else torch.tensor(float('-inf'), device=self.model.device)
1771        nmax_cand = ( log_fmax / torch.abs(torch.log(x_max))) if (x_max > 1) else torch.tensor(float('inf'),  device=self.model.device)
1772
1773        # Use physically-derived overflow bounds directly; fall back to ±100 if infinite
1774        # (nmin_cand is -inf when x_min >= 1; nmax_cand is +inf when x_max <= 1)
1775        nmin = torch.where(torch.isfinite(nmin_cand), nmin_cand, torch.tensor(-100.0, device=self.model.device))
1776        nmax = torch.where(torch.isfinite(nmax_cand), nmax_cand, torch.tensor( 100.0, device=self.model.device))
1777        # ensure proper ordering just in case
1778        nmin = torch.minimum(nmin, nmax)
1779
1780        # CRITICAL: Use meta_subset (correctly ordered) instead of full self.model.meta
1781        guides_tensor = torch.tensor(meta_subset['guide_code'].values, dtype=torch.long, device=self.model.device)
1782
1783        # Distribution-specific normalization for data-driven priors
1784        # For building priors later:
1785        y_obs_for_prior = None
1786
1787        # Note: min_denominator is now required for binomial/multinomial (validated earlier)
1788        # For negbinom/normal/studentt, it's not used so None is fine
1789
1790        if distribution == 'binomial' and denominator_tensor is not None:
1791            # Full probabilities for the likelihood
1792            y_obs_factored = y_obs_tensor / denominator_tensor.clamp_min(epsilon_tensor)
1793
1794            # Store valid_mask for later (will apply AFTER technical correction)
1795            valid_mask_binomial = (denominator_tensor >= min_denominator)
1796            print(f"[INFO] Binomial: will use {valid_mask_binomial.float().mean().item()*100:.1f}% of entries with denominator >= {min_denominator} for priors (after technical correction)")
1797
1798            # Don't create y_obs_for_prior yet - technical correction happens first
1799            y_obs_for_prior = y_obs_factored
1800
1801        elif distribution == 'multinomial' and y_obs_tensor.ndim == 3:
1802            total_counts = y_obs_tensor.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(epsilon_tensor)  # [N, T, 1]
1803            y_obs_factored = y_obs_tensor / total_counts  # [N, T, K]
1804
1805            # Store valid_mask for later (will apply AFTER technical correction)
1806            valid_mask_multinomial = (total_counts >= min_denominator)  # [N, T, 1]
1807            print(f"[INFO] Multinomial: will use {valid_mask_multinomial.float().mean().item()*100:.1f}% of entries with total counts >= {min_denominator} for priors (after technical correction)")
1808
1809            # Don't create y_obs_for_prior yet - technical correction happens first
1810            y_obs_for_prior = y_obs_factored
1811
1812        elif sum_factor_col is not None:
1813            y_obs_factored = y_obs_tensor / sum_factor_tensor.view(-1, 1)
1814            y_obs_for_prior = y_obs_factored
1815        else:
1816            y_obs_factored = y_obs_tensor
1817            y_obs_for_prior = y_obs_factored
1818
1819        # ---- Multinomial zero-category mask (analogous to fit_ntc zero_cat_mask) ----
1820        # Identifies categories structurally absent across ALL trans cells.
1821        # These phantom positions are already masked inline inside _model_y; this block
1822        # performs an early diagnostic check and warns when features have ≤1 active
1823        # category (which should have been filtered at Modality initialisation).
1824        if distribution == 'multinomial' and y_obs_tensor.ndim == 3:
1825            _obs_total_per_cat = y_obs_tensor.sum(dim=0)  # [T, K]
1826            zero_cat_mask_trans = (_obs_total_per_cat == 0)  # [T, K] bool
1827            _active_k = (~zero_cat_mask_trans).sum(dim=-1)  # [T]
1828            if (_active_k <= 1).any():
1829                import warnings as _warnings
1830                _bad_t = torch.nonzero(_active_k <= 1, as_tuple=False).squeeze(-1).tolist()
1831                _warnings.warn(
1832                    f"[fit_trans] {len(_bad_t)} multinomial feature(s) have ≤1 active "
1833                    f"category in the trans data (feature indices: "
1834                    f"{_bad_t[:10]}{'...' if len(_bad_t) > 10 else ''}). "
1835                    f"These features should be filtered before fitting (at Modality "
1836                    f"initialisation). Fitting will be unreliable for these features.",
1837                    UserWarning,
1838                    stacklevel=3,
1839                )
1840        else:
1841            zero_cat_mask_trans = None
1842
1843        # ===================================================================
1844        # CORRECT FOR TECHNICAL EFFECTS BEFORE COMPUTING PRIORS
1845        # ===================================================================
1846        # Remove technical batch effects from observed data before computing A and Vmax priors.
1847        if alpha_y_prefit is not None and groups_tensor is not None:
1848            print(f"[INFO] Correcting for technical effects before computing priors (distribution: {distribution})")
1849
1850            # alpha_y_prefit is always [C, T] (point estimate/mean), index groups dimension
1851            alpha_y_expanded = alpha_y_prefit[groups_tensor, ...]  # [N, T] or [N, T, K]
1852
1853            # alpha_y_expanded is now [N, T] (or [N, T, K] for multinomial), matching y_obs_for_prior
1854            # NO TRANSPOSE NEEDED - both are [N, T]
1855
1856            # Check alpha_y_expanded for issues
1857            if not torch.isfinite(alpha_y_expanded).all():
1858                n_invalid_alpha = (~torch.isfinite(alpha_y_expanded)).sum().item()
1859                print(f"[WARNING] alpha_y_expanded contains {n_invalid_alpha} non-finite values before correction")
1860            elif distribution == 'binomial':
1861                alpha_mean = alpha_y_expanded.mean().item()
1862                if abs(alpha_mean - 1.0) < 0.5:
1863                    print(f"[WARNING] alpha_y_expanded looks like multiplicative correction (mean~1.0). "
1864                          f"For binomial, expected additive correction on logit scale (mean~0, range~[-5,5]). "
1865                          f"You may be using technical fit results from old (buggy) code. "
1866                          f"Re-run fit_ntc with the fixed code.")
1867
1868            if distribution == 'negbinom':
1869                # Technical effect: multiplicative (mu_corrected = mu * alpha_y_mult)
1870                # Inverse: divide by alpha_y_mult to get baseline
1871                # alpha_y_prefit for negbinom is multiplicative (from fit_ntc)
1872                y_obs_for_prior = y_obs_for_prior / alpha_y_expanded.clamp_min(epsilon_tensor)
1873                print(f"[INFO] negbinom: Applied inverse multiplicative correction (divide by alpha_y_mult)")
1874
1875            elif distribution in ['normal', 'studentt']:
1876                # Technical effect: additive (mu_corrected = mu + alpha_y_add)
1877                # Inverse: subtract alpha_y_add to get baseline
1878                # alpha_y_prefit for normal/studentt is additive (from fit_ntc)
1879                y_obs_for_prior = y_obs_for_prior - alpha_y_expanded
1880                print(f"[INFO] {distribution}: Applied inverse additive correction (subtract alpha_y_add)")
1881
1882            elif distribution == 'binomial':
1883                # Technical effect: logit scale (logit(p_corrected) = logit(p) + alpha_y_add)
1884                # Inverse: logit(p_baseline) = logit(p_observed) - alpha_y_add
1885                # Then: p_baseline = sigmoid(logit(p_baseline))
1886
1887                # Convert observed proportions to logit scale
1888                p_obs_clamped = torch.clamp(y_obs_for_prior, min=epsilon_tensor, max=1.0 - epsilon_tensor)
1889                logit_obs = torch.log(p_obs_clamped) - torch.log(1.0 - p_obs_clamped)
1890
1891                # Apply inverse correction on logit scale
1892                logit_baseline = logit_obs - alpha_y_expanded
1893                if not torch.isfinite(logit_baseline).all():
1894                    n_invalid = (~torch.isfinite(logit_baseline)).sum().item()
1895                    print(f"[WARNING] logit_baseline contains {n_invalid} non-finite values after correction")
1896
1897                # Convert back to probability scale
1898                y_obs_for_prior = torch.sigmoid(logit_baseline)
1899                print(f"[INFO] binomial: Applied inverse logit correction (subtract alpha_y_add on logit scale)")
1900
1901            elif distribution == 'multinomial':
1902                # Technical effect: log scale (log(probs_corrected) = log(probs) + alpha_y_add)
1903                # Inverse: log(probs_baseline) = log(probs_observed) - alpha_y_add
1904                # Then: probs_baseline = exp(log_probs_baseline) / sum(exp(...))
1905                # For multinomial, alpha_y_expanded is already [N, T, K] from above (matches y_obs_for_prior)
1906
1907                # Convert observed proportions to log scale
1908                p_obs_clamped = torch.clamp(y_obs_for_prior, min=epsilon_tensor)
1909                log_probs_obs = torch.log(p_obs_clamped)
1910
1911                # Apply inverse correction on log scale
1912                log_probs_baseline = log_probs_obs - alpha_y_expanded
1913
1914                # Normalize (softmax) to get valid probabilities
1915                y_obs_for_prior = torch.softmax(log_probs_baseline, dim=-1)
1916                print(f"[INFO] multinomial: Applied inverse log correction (subtract alpha_y_add on log scale)")
1917
1918            # Handle any NaN or invalid values that may result from correction
1919            # (e.g., if correction pushes values outside valid range)
1920            if not torch.isfinite(y_obs_for_prior).all():
1921                n_invalid = (~torch.isfinite(y_obs_for_prior)).sum().item()
1922                n_total = y_obs_for_prior.numel()
1923                print(f"[WARNING] Technical correction produced {n_invalid}/{n_total} "
1924                      f"({100*n_invalid/n_total:.2f}%) non-finite values. "
1925                      f"These will be excluded from prior computation.")
1926                # Mark invalid values as NaN so they're excluded by nanmean/nanvar
1927                y_obs_for_prior = torch.where(
1928                    torch.isfinite(y_obs_for_prior),
1929                    y_obs_for_prior,
1930                    torch.full_like(y_obs_for_prior, float('nan'))
1931                )
1932        else:
1933            if alpha_y_prefit is not None:
1934                print(f"[INFO] alpha_y_prefit provided but groups_tensor is None - skipping technical correction")
1935
1936        # NOW apply min_denominator masking (AFTER technical correction)
1937        # This prevents computing priors from low-coverage observations
1938        if distribution == 'binomial' and 'valid_mask_binomial' in locals():
1939            # Mask low-coverage entries with NaN
1940            y_obs_for_prior = torch.where(
1941                valid_mask_binomial,
1942                y_obs_for_prior,
1943                torch.full_like(y_obs_for_prior, float('nan'))
1944            )
1945            n_masked = (~valid_mask_binomial).sum().item()
1946            n_total = valid_mask_binomial.numel()
1947            print(f"[INFO] Masked {n_masked}/{n_total} ({100*n_masked/n_total:.2f}%) low-coverage observations (denominator < {min_denominator})")
1948
1949        elif distribution == 'multinomial' and 'valid_mask_multinomial' in locals():
1950            # Mask low-coverage entries with NaN
1951            y_obs_for_prior = torch.where(
1952                valid_mask_multinomial,
1953                y_obs_for_prior,
1954                torch.full_like(y_obs_for_prior, float('nan'))
1955            )
1956            n_masked = (~valid_mask_multinomial).sum().item()
1957            n_total = valid_mask_multinomial.numel()
1958            print(f"[INFO] Masked {n_masked}/{n_total} ({100*n_masked/n_total:.2f}%) low-coverage observations (total counts < {min_denominator})")
1959
1960        unique_guides = torch.unique(guides_tensor)
1961
1962        # Pre-extract q01 of NTC posterior means for the Q05=0 floor below.
1963        # Only needed for negbinom/binomial; full NTC anchor extraction happens later.
1964        _q01_ntc_for_floor = None
1965        if distribution in ('negbinom', 'binomial'):
1966            _post_tech_pre = getattr(modality, 'posterior_samples_ntc', None)
1967            if _post_tech_pre is not None and 'mu_ntc' in _post_tech_pre:
1968                try:
1969                    _mu_ntc_pre = _post_tech_pre['mu_ntc']
1970                    if not torch.is_tensor(_mu_ntc_pre):
1971                        _mu_ntc_pre = torch.tensor(_mu_ntc_pre, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
1972                    else:
1973                        _mu_ntc_pre = _mu_ntc_pre.float().to(self.model.device)
1974                    _mu_ntc_pre_flat = _mu_ntc_pre
1975                    while _mu_ntc_pre_flat.ndim > 1:
1976                        _mu_ntc_pre_flat = _mu_ntc_pre_flat.median(dim=0).values
1977                    _finite_pre = _mu_ntc_pre_flat[(_mu_ntc_pre_flat > 0) & ~torch.isnan(_mu_ntc_pre_flat)]
1978                    if _finite_pre.numel() > 0:
1979                        _q01_ntc_for_floor = torch.quantile(_finite_pre, 0.01)
1980                except Exception:
1981                    pass
1982
1983        # Compute cell-level Q05/Q95 for Amean/Vmax priors (always, regardless of guide count)
1984        _q05_was_zero = None
1985        mean_y_corrected_tensor = None  # [T]; set below for 2D distributions (negbinom, binomial)
1986        if y_obs_for_prior.ndim == 2:  # [N, T]
1987            Amean_tensor = torch.nanquantile(y_obs_for_prior, 0.05, dim=0)  # [T]
1988            Vmax_raw     = torch.nanquantile(y_obs_for_prior, 0.95, dim=0)  # [T]
1989            _y_mean  = torch.nanmean(y_obs_for_prior, dim=0)                # [T]
1990            _y_dev   = y_obs_for_prior - _y_mean.unsqueeze(0)               # [N, T]
1991            _n_valid = (~torch.isnan(y_obs_for_prior)).sum(dim=0).clamp_min(2)  # [T]
1992            cell_var = torch.where(
1993                _n_valid >= 2,
1994                torch.nansum(_y_dev ** 2, dim=0) / (_n_valid - 1).float(),
1995                torch.full((T,), float('nan'), device=self.model.device)
1996            )  # [T]
1997
1998            # Q05=0 floor: for count/proportion distributions (negbinom, binomial), Q05=0
1999            # means the gene is sparse and needs a small positive lower bound because the
2000            # negbinom A prior uses log2(Amean/2), which requires Amean > 0.
2001            # Use a fixed small constant (2^-10 ≈ 1e-3 normalized counts) rather than the
2002            # data-driven min non-zero Q05, which can be inflated (~0.5–1 count) and would
2003            # wrongly pull the prior lower bound above the NTC expression level for sparse genes.
2004            # The y_ntc anchor provides the upper reference; Amean just needs a valid lower bound.
2005            #
2006            # For normal/studentt, Q05 can legitimately be ≤ 0 (e.g. negative SpliZ scores),
2007            # and the linear-space prior works fine with negative Amean — so only floor NaNs.
2008            # NaN Amean values (no valid observations) are handled by the fallback below.
2009            if distribution in ('negbinom', 'binomial'):
2010                _q05_was_zero = (Amean_tensor <= 0) | torch.isnan(Amean_tensor)
2011            else:  # normal, studentt: Q05 can be ≤ 0; only catch NaN
2012                _q05_was_zero = torch.isnan(Amean_tensor)
2013            if _q05_was_zero.any():
2014                n_q05_zero = _q05_was_zero.sum().item()
2015                _amean_floor = self._t(2.0 ** -10)
2016                if _q01_ntc_for_floor is not None:
2017                    _amean_floor = torch.minimum(_q01_ntc_for_floor, _amean_floor)
2018                Amean_tensor = torch.where(_q05_was_zero, _amean_floor.expand_as(Amean_tensor), Amean_tensor)
2019                print(f"[INFO] Q05 floor: {n_q05_zero} features raised to {_amean_floor.item():.3e} (min(q01_ntc, 2^-10))")
2020            Amean_tensor     = Amean_tensor.clamp_min(self._t(1e-12))
2021            Vmax_mean_tensor = (Vmax_raw - Amean_tensor).clamp_min(self._t(1e-3))
2022
2023            # Mean across all cells — used as a data-driven floor for the A prior upper
2024            # anchor. When y_ntc ≈ 0 (gene absent in NTC but expressed in perturbations),
2025            # this prevents both anchors collapsing to the same floor value.
2026            mean_y_corrected_tensor = torch.nanmean(y_obs_for_prior, dim=0).clamp_min(self._t(1e-12))  # [T]
2027
2028        elif y_obs_for_prior.ndim == 3:  # [N, T, K] — multinomial
2029            K_obs = y_obs_for_prior.shape[2]
2030            _y3   = y_obs_for_prior.reshape(N, T * K_obs)             # [N, T*K]
2031            _Amean_flat = torch.nanquantile(_y3, 0.05, dim=0)         # [T*K]
2032            _Vmax_flat  = torch.nanquantile(_y3, 0.95, dim=0)         # [T*K]
2033            _y3_mean    = torch.nanmean(_y3, dim=0)                   # [T*K]
2034            _y3_dev     = _y3 - _y3_mean.unsqueeze(0)                 # [N, T*K]
2035            _n3_valid   = (~torch.isnan(_y3)).sum(dim=0).clamp_min(2) # [T*K]
2036            _var3_flat  = torch.where(
2037                _n3_valid >= 2,
2038                torch.nansum(_y3_dev ** 2, dim=0) / (_n3_valid - 1).float(),
2039                torch.full((T * K_obs,), float('nan'), device=self.model.device)
2040            )  # [T*K]
2041            Amean_tensor = _Amean_flat.reshape(T, K_obs)  # [T, K]
2042            Vmax_raw     = _Vmax_flat.reshape(T, K_obs)   # [T, K]
2043            cell_var     = _var3_flat.reshape(T, K_obs)   # [T, K]
2044            # Q05=0 floor: use fixed small constant (proportions clamped at 1e-3 below anyway).
2045            _q05_was_zero = (Amean_tensor <= 0) | torch.isnan(Amean_tensor)
2046            if _q05_was_zero.any():
2047                n_q05_zero = _q05_was_zero.sum().item()
2048                _amean_floor_mn = self._t(2.0 ** -10)
2049                Amean_tensor = torch.where(_q05_was_zero, _amean_floor_mn.expand_as(Amean_tensor), Amean_tensor)
2050                print(f"[INFO] Q05=0 floor (multinomial): {n_q05_zero} (feature, category) cells raised to 2^-10={2.0**-10:.3e}")
2051            Amean_tensor     = Amean_tensor.clamp_min(self._t(1e-12))   # [T, K]
2052            Vmax_mean_tensor = (Vmax_raw - Amean_tensor).clamp_min(self._t(1e-3))
2053
2054        # For binomial/multinomial: clamp Vmax_mean to valid Beta range
2055        if distribution in ['binomial', 'multinomial']:
2056            Vmax_mean_tensor = Vmax_mean_tensor.clamp(min=self._t(1e-3), max=self._t(1.0 - 1e-6))
2057            Amean_tensor = Amean_tensor.clamp(min=self._t(1e-3), max=self._t(1.0 - 1e-6))
2058
2059        # Handle NaN values (features where ALL observations were filtered out)
2060        nan_mask = torch.isnan(Amean_tensor) | torch.isnan(Vmax_mean_tensor)
2061        if nan_mask.any():
2062            n_nan = nan_mask.sum().item() if nan_mask.ndim == 1 else nan_mask.any(dim=-1).sum().item()
2063            print(f"[WARNING] {n_nan} features have all observations filtered (denominator < {min_denominator}). Using fallback values.")
2064
2065            # Fallback: median of valid Amean/cell_var across features
2066            if distribution in ['binomial', 'multinomial']:
2067                valid_A   = Amean_tensor[~torch.isnan(Amean_tensor)]
2068                valid_var = cell_var[~torch.isnan(cell_var)]
2069                if valid_A.numel() > 0:
2070                    valid_mean    = torch.median(valid_A)
2071                    valid_var_val = torch.median(valid_var) if valid_var.numel() > 0 else self._t(0.1)
2072                else:
2073                    print("[WARNING] No valid observations found! Using generic defaults: A=0.3, var=0.1")
2074                    valid_mean    = self._t(0.3)
2075                    valid_var_val = self._t(0.1)
2076                print(f"[INFO] Using fallback: mean={valid_mean.item():.3f}, var={valid_var_val.item():.3f}")
2077                fallback_A    = torch.clamp(valid_mean * 0.5, min=0.01, max=0.99)
2078                fallback_Vmax = torch.clamp(valid_mean,       min=0.01, max=0.99)
2079            else:  # negbinom, normal, studentt
2080                valid_A   = Amean_tensor[~torch.isnan(Amean_tensor)]
2081                valid_var = cell_var[~torch.isnan(cell_var)]
2082                if valid_A.numel() > 0:
2083                    valid_mean    = torch.median(valid_A)
2084                    valid_var_val = torch.median(valid_var) if valid_var.numel() > 0 else valid_mean * 0.5
2085                else:
2086                    print("[WARNING] No valid observations found! Using generic defaults: A=5.0, var=5.0")
2087                    valid_mean    = self._t(5.0)
2088                    valid_var_val = self._t(5.0)
2089                print(f"[INFO] Using fallback: mean={valid_mean.item():.3f}, var={valid_var_val.item():.3f}")
2090                fallback_A    = torch.clamp(valid_mean * 0.5, min=1e-3)
2091                fallback_Vmax = torch.clamp(valid_mean,       min=1e-3)
2092
2093            Amean_tensor = torch.where(
2094                torch.isnan(Amean_tensor), torch.full_like(Amean_tensor, fallback_A), Amean_tensor)
2095            Vmax_mean_tensor = torch.where(
2096                torch.isnan(Vmax_mean_tensor), torch.full_like(Vmax_mean_tensor, fallback_Vmax), Vmax_mean_tensor)
2097
2098        # --- A prior: NTC anchor (all distributions) ---
2099        # Extract y_ntc_tensor (posterior mean of NTC expression per feature) to anchor the
2100        # noisy-feature end of the A prior in _model_y, preventing A-collapse.
2101        # For negbinom: also floors Amean at q01(mu_ntc) to prevent near-zero Q05 estimates.
2102        # Keys per distribution:
2103        #   negbinom/normal/studentt/binomial: posterior_samples_ntc['mu_ntc']  → [S, T]
2104        #   multinomial:                       posterior_samples_ntc['probs_baseline'] → [S, T, K]
2105        y_ntc_tensor = None
2106        _post_tech = getattr(modality, 'posterior_samples_ntc', None)
2107        if _post_tech is not None:
2108            try:
2109                if distribution in ('negbinom', 'normal', 'studentt', 'binomial') and 'mu_ntc' in _post_tech:
2110                    _mu_ntc = _post_tech['mu_ntc']
2111                    if not torch.is_tensor(_mu_ntc):
2112                        _mu_ntc = torch.tensor(_mu_ntc, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
2113                    else:
2114                        _mu_ntc = _mu_ntc.float().to(self.model.device)
2115                    # Collapse any leading dimensions (samples, groups, etc.) so that
2116                    # _mu_ntc ends up as [T] regardless of whether it is stored as
2117                    # [S, T], [S, C, T], or already [T].
2118                    if _mu_ntc.ndim > 1 and _mu_ntc.shape[-1] == T:
2119                        # Flatten all leading dims by successive mean over dim=0
2120                        _mu_ntc_flat = _mu_ntc
2121                        while _mu_ntc_flat.ndim > 1:
2122                            _mu_ntc_flat = _mu_ntc_flat.median(dim=0).values
2123                        if distribution == 'negbinom':
2124                            n_nonpos = (_mu_ntc_flat <= 0).sum().item()
2125                            if n_nonpos > 0:
2126                                print(f"[DEBUG] {n_nonpos}/{T} genes have mean mu_ntc ≤ 0 "
2127                                      f"(min={_mu_ntc_flat.min().item():.3e}); possible float32 underflow in NTC posterior")
2128                        y_ntc_tensor = _mu_ntc_flat  # [T]
2129                        # Compute q01_ntc_global BEFORE NaN fill: 1st percentile of per-gene NTC means
2130                        # across genes where fit_ntc was run (ignores NaN genes).
2131                        _finite_ntc = _mu_ntc_flat[~torch.isnan(_mu_ntc_flat)]
2132                        q01_ntc_global = torch.quantile(_finite_ntc, 0.01) if _finite_ntc.numel() > 0 else None
2133                        # NaN fill: genes where fit_ntc was not run get q01_ntc_global as anchor
2134                        _ntc_nan_mask = torch.isnan(y_ntc_tensor)
2135                        if _ntc_nan_mask.any():
2136                            n_ntc_nan = _ntc_nan_mask.sum().item()
2137                            if q01_ntc_global is not None:
2138                                print(f"[WARNING] {n_ntc_nan}/{T} genes have NaN mu_ntc (fit_ntc not run); "
2139                                      f"using q01_ntc_global={q01_ntc_global.item():.3e} as y_ntc anchor")
2140                                y_ntc_tensor = torch.where(_ntc_nan_mask, q01_ntc_global.expand_as(y_ntc_tensor), y_ntc_tensor)
2141                            else:
2142                                print(f"[WARNING] {n_ntc_nan}/{T} genes have NaN mu_ntc and no finite NTC posterior; "
2143                                      f"using Amean as y_ntc fallback")
2144                                y_ntc_tensor = torch.where(_ntc_nan_mask, Amean_tensor, y_ntc_tensor)
2145                        if distribution == 'negbinom':
2146                            if (y_ntc_tensor <= 0).any():
2147                                raise ValueError(

2149                                    f"(min={y_ntc_tensor.min().item():.3e}). "

2151                                )

2155                        q01_ntc_global = torch.quantile(_finite_ntc_1d, 0.01) if _finite_ntc_1d.numel() > 0 else None

2157                        if _ntc_nan_mask.any():
2158                            n_ntc_nan = _ntc_nan_mask.sum().item()
2159                            if q01_ntc_global is not None:
2160                                print(f"[WARNING] {n_ntc_nan}/{T} genes have NaN mu_ntc (fit_ntc not run); "
2161                                      f"using q01_ntc_global={q01_ntc_global.item():.3e} as y_ntc anchor")
2162                                y_ntc_tensor = torch.where(_ntc_nan_mask, q01_ntc_global.expand_as(y_ntc_tensor), y_ntc_tensor)
2163                            else:
2164                                print(f"[WARNING] {n_ntc_nan}/{T} genes have NaN mu_ntc and no finite NTC posterior; "
2165                                      f"using Amean as y_ntc fallback")
2166                                y_ntc_tensor = torch.where(_ntc_nan_mask, Amean_tensor, y_ntc_tensor)
2167                        if distribution == 'negbinom':
2168                            if (y_ntc_tensor <= 0).any():
2169                                raise ValueError(
2170                                    f"y_ntc_tensor contains non-positive values "
2171                                    f"(min={y_ntc_tensor.min().item():.3e}). "
2172                                    f"mu_ntc posterior has strictly positive support — this should not occur."
2173                                )
2174                    else:
2175                        print(f"[WARNING] mu_ntc shape {tuple(_mu_ntc.shape)} doesn't match T={T}; skipping A prior NTC anchor")

2177                    _probs = _post_tech['probs_baseline']
2178                    if not torch.is_tensor(_probs):
2179                        _probs = torch.tensor(_probs, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.model.device)
2180                    else:
2181                        _probs = _probs.float().to(self.model.device)
2182                    _probs_flat = None
2183                    if _probs.ndim == 3 and _probs.shape[1] == T:
2184                        _probs_flat = _probs.median(dim=0).values  # [T, K]
2185                    elif _probs.ndim == 2 and _probs.shape[0] == T:
2186                        _probs_flat = _probs              # [T, K]
2187                    else:
2188                        print(f"[WARNING] probs_baseline shape {tuple(_probs.shape)} doesn't match T={T}; skipping multinomial NTC anchor")

2192                        if _valid_rows.any():

2195                            q01_ntc_global_probs = q01_ntc_global_probs / q01_ntc_global_probs.sum().clamp_min(1e-10)
2196                        else:

2200                        _ntc_nan_mask = torch.isnan(_probs_flat).all(dim=-1)  # [T]
2201                        if _ntc_nan_mask.any():

2204                                  f"using q01_ntc_global probability vector as y_ntc anchor")

2257                      f"falling back to sampled o_y for A prior weight")

2456        def _load_and_validate_ckpt(path, context="loading checkpoint"):
2457            """Load checkpoint and validate structural metadata against current call."""
2458            try:
2459                ckpt = torch.load(path, map_location=self.model.device, weights_only=False)
2460            except Exception as e:
2461                print(f"[WARNING] Could not load checkpoint ({e}): {path}")
2462                return None
2463            # Structural mismatches → error (param shapes won't match)
2464            _bad = []
2465            for key, expected, label in [
2466                ('N', N, 'number of cells'),
2467                ('T', T, 'number of features'),
2468                ('K', K, 'number of categories (K)'),
2469                ('C', C, 'number of technical groups (C)'),
2470            ]:
2471                stored = ckpt.get(key)
2472                if stored is not None and stored != expected:
2473                    _bad.append(f"  {label}: checkpoint={stored}, current call={expected}")
2474            if _bad:
2475                raise ValueError(
2476                    f"[{context}] Checkpoint metadata mismatch — cannot resume "
2477                    f"(parameter shapes differ):\n" + "\n".join(_bad)
2478                )

2480            # Use effective_function_type when available (warmup checkpoints store

2483            if _stored_ft is not None and _stored_ft != function_type:
2484                warnings.warn(
2485                    f"[{context}] function_type mismatch: checkpoint effective={_stored_ft!r}, "
2486                    f"current call={function_type!r}. Ensure model and guide are compatible."
2487                )
2488            _stored_dist = ckpt.get('distribution')
2489            if _stored_dist is not None and _stored_dist != distribution:
2490                warnings.warn(
2491                    f"[{context}] distribution mismatch: checkpoint={_stored_dist!r}, "
2492                    f"current call={distribution!r}."
2493                )
2494            return ckpt

2534                    (checkpoint_path, 'primary (_latest.pt)'),
2535                    (_tmp_path,       '.tmp (rename interrupted)'),
2536                    (_backup_path,    '.bak (previous interval)'),
2537                ]:

2539                        print(f"[INFO] Attempting to load {_label}: {os.path.basename(_cand)}")
2540                        _ckpt = _load_and_validate_ckpt(_cand, context="resume")

2990                if y_ntc_tensor is not None:
2991                    _y_ntc_np = y_ntc_tensor.cpu().numpy()
2992                    # Mirror _model_y: lift upper anchor to mean(y_corrected) when y_ntc < mean.
2993                    if mean_y_corrected_tensor is not None:
2994                        _mean_ycorr_np = mean_y_corrected_tensor.cpu().numpy()
2995                        _upper_np = np.maximum(_y_ntc_np, _mean_ycorr_np)
2996                    else:
2997                        _upper_np = _y_ntc_np
2998                    _log2_upper = np.log2(np.maximum(_upper_np, 1e-12))
2999                    _log2_lower = np.maximum(
3000                        np.log2(np.maximum(_Amean_np / 2.0, 1e-12)),
3001                        _log2_upper - 4.0,
3002                    )
3003                    _sigma_log2_A = np.clip(_log2_upper - _log2_lower, 1.0, 4.0)
3004                    if o_y_ntc_tensor is not None:
3005                        _prior_mean_oy = float((beta_o_beta_tensor / beta_o_alpha_tensor)
3006                                               .clamp_min(epsilon_tensor).item())
3007                        _w = (o_y_ntc_tensor / (o_y_ntc_tensor + _prior_mean_oy)).cpu().numpy()
3008                    else:
3009                        _w = np.zeros_like(_Amean_np)
3010                    _mu_log2_A = (1.0 - _w) * _log2_lower + _w * _log2_upper
3011                else:
3012                    _mu_log2_A    = np.log2(np.maximum(_Amean_np / 2.0, 1e-12))
3013                    _sigma_log2_A = np.full_like(_mu_log2_A, 4.0)
3014                trans_prior_params['A_log2_mu']    = _mu_log2_A    # [T]
3015                trans_prior_params['A_log2_sigma'] = _sigma_log2_A  # [T]
3016
3017        # Store results
3018        # Store in modality
3019        modality.posterior_samples_trans = posterior_samples_y
3020        modality.trans_prior_params = trans_prior_params
3021        modality.losses_trans = self.losses_trans  # Store loss history
3022
3023        # For primary modality, also store at model level for direct access via model.posterior_samples_trans
3024        if modality_name == self.model.primary_modality:
3025            self.model.posterior_samples_trans = posterior_samples_y
3026            self.model.losses_trans = self.losses_trans
3027            self.model.trans_prior_params = trans_prior_params
3028            # NOTE: alpha_y_prefit is stored per-modality (already done above), not at model level
3029            print(f"[INFO] Stored results in modality '{modality_name}' and at model level (primary modality)")
3030        else:
3031            print(f"[INFO] Stored results in modality '{modality_name}'")
3032
3033        if self.model.device.type == "cuda":
3034            torch.cuda.empty_cache()

3036        gc.collect()
3037        pyro.clear_param_store()

3039        # Remove the rolling checkpoint (_latest.pt) and its temporaries now that
3040        # results are stored on the model.  Numbered (_step*.pt), warmup, and
3041        # complete checkpoints are retained for post-hoc analysis.
3042        if checkpoint_path is not None and not _predictive_only_mode:
3043            for _p in [checkpoint_path, checkpoint_path + '.bak', checkpoint_path + '.tmp']:
3044                if os.path.exists(_p):
3045                    os.remove(_p)

3047                  f"numbered/warmup/complete checkpoints retained in "
3048                  f"{os.path.dirname(checkpoint_path)}")
3049
3050        print("Finished fit_trans.")
class TransFitter: 
  51class TransFitter:
  52    """Handles trans effects fitting."""
  53
  54    def _save_checkpoint_atomic(self, checkpoint_path: str, data: dict) -> None:
  55        """Write checkpoint atomically (tmp → rename) and keep previous as .bak.
  56
  57        Three-step protocol:
  58          1. torch.save  →  <path>.tmp        (new data, not yet visible)
  59          2. os.replace  old <path>  →  .bak  (old data safely preserved)
  60          3. os.replace  .tmp  →  <path>      (atomic on POSIX; new data visible)
  61
  62        Failure modes:
  63          Die in step 1 (during write): .tmp corrupt, <path> unchanged → resume loads <path>.
  64          Die between 1 and 2: .tmp complete, <path> unchanged → resume loads <path>.
  65          Die between 2 and 3: .tmp complete, <path> gone (→ .bak) → resume tries .tmp
  66                                first (complete), falls back to .bak (one interval behind).
  67          Die during step 3:  os.replace is atomic on POSIX → either completes or not,
  68                              leaving either <path> or .tmp visible; .bak always intact.
  69        """
  70        backup_path = checkpoint_path + '.bak'
  71        tmp_path = checkpoint_path + '.tmp'
  72        torch.save(data, tmp_path)
  73        if os.path.exists(checkpoint_path):
  74            os.replace(checkpoint_path, backup_path)
  75        os.replace(tmp_path, checkpoint_path)
  76

  85        """
  86        self.model = model
