  99    def _tensor_summary(self, x: torch.Tensor):
 100        x_det = x.detach()
 101        finite = torch.isfinite(x_det)
 102        n = x_det.numel()
 103        n_bad = (~finite).sum().item()
 104        n_nan = torch.isnan(x_det).sum().item()
 105        n_inf = torch.isinf(x_det).sum().item()
 106        if finite.any():
 107            x_f = x_det[finite]
 108            mn = x_f.min().item()
 109            mx = x_f.max().item()
 110            mean = x_f.mean().item()
 111            std = x_f.std().item()
 112        else:
 113            mn = mx = mean = std = float("nan")
 114        return dict(n=n, n_bad=n_bad, n_nan=n_nan, n_inf=n_inf, min=mn, max=mx, mean=mean, std=std)
 115
 116    def _print_tensor(self, name: str, x: torch.Tensor, prefix=""):
 117        s = self._tensor_summary(x)
 118        print(
 119            f"{prefix}{name}: shape={tuple(x.shape)} dtype={x.dtype} device={x.device} "
 120            f"bad={s['n_bad']}/{s['n']} (nan={s['n_nan']}, inf={s['n_inf']}) "
 121            f"min={s['min']:.3g} max={s['max']:.3g} mean={s['mean']:.3g} std={s['std']:.3g}"
 122        )
 123
 124    def _check_param_store_all(self, step: int, svi=None, where="", prev_finite=None, verbose_on_change=True):
 125        store = pyro.get_param_store()
 126        if prev_finite is None:
 127            prev_finite = {}
 128
 129        changed = []
 130        bad_vals = []
 131        bad_grads = []
 132
 133        for name, p in store.items():
 134            if not isinstance(p, torch.Tensor):
 135                continue
 136
 137            now_finite = torch.isfinite(p).all().item()
 138            was_finite = prev_finite.get(name, True)
 139            prev_finite[name] = now_finite
 140
 141            if was_finite and (not now_finite):
 142                changed.append(name)
 143
 144            if not now_finite:
 145                bad_vals.append(name)
 146
 147            if p.grad is not None and (not torch.isfinite(p.grad).all().item()):
 148                bad_grads.append(name)
 149
 150        if changed and verbose_on_change:
 151            print(f"\n[ERROR] Param(s) flipped finite→nonfinite at step {step} {where}: {changed}")
 152            for n in changed:
 153                self._print_tensor(n, store[n], prefix="  ")
 154                if store[n].grad is not None:
 155                    self._print_tensor(n + ".grad", store[n].grad, prefix="  ")
 156
 157        if bad_vals and verbose_on_change and not changed:
 158            print(f"\n[ERROR] Non-finite param value(s) present at step {step} {where}: "
 159                  f"{bad_vals[:10]}{'...' if len(bad_vals)>10 else ''}")
 160            for n in bad_vals[:10]:
 161                self._print_tensor(n, store[n], prefix="  ")
 162
 163        if bad_grads and verbose_on_change:
 164            print(f"\n[ERROR] Non-finite gradient(s) present at step {step} {where}: "
 165                  f"{bad_grads[:10]}{'...' if len(bad_grads)>10 else ''}")
 166            for n in bad_grads[:10]:
 167                if store[n].grad is not None:
 168                    self._print_tensor(n + ".grad", store[n].grad, prefix="  ")
 169
 170        # Best-effort optimizer-state check (optional)
 171        if svi is not None and hasattr(svi, "optim"):
 172            opt = svi.optim
 173            optim_objs = getattr(opt, "optim_objs", None)
 174            if isinstance(optim_objs, dict):
 175                bad_state = []
 176                for pname, torch_opt in optim_objs.items():
 177                    base_opt = getattr(torch_opt, "optimizer", torch_opt)
 178                    if not hasattr(base_opt, "state"):
 179                        continue
 180                    for group in base_opt.param_groups:
 181                        for param in group.get("params", []):
 182                            st = base_opt.state.get(param, {})
 183                            for key, val in st.items():
 184                                if torch.is_tensor(val) and (not torch.isfinite(val).all().item()):
 185                                    bad_state.append((pname, key))
 186                if bad_state and verbose_on_change:
 187                    print(f"\n[ERROR] Non-finite optimizer state at step {step} {where}: "
 188                          f"{bad_state[:10]}{'...' if len(bad_state)>10 else ''}")
 189
 190        any_bad = bool(bad_vals or bad_grads)
 191        return prev_finite, any_bad
 192
 193    def _collect_dist_tensors(self, fn):
 194        tensors = []
 195        if isinstance(fn, dist.TransformedDistribution):
 196            tensors += self._collect_dist_tensors(fn.base_dist)
 197            return tensors
 198
 199        for attr in [
 200            "loc", "scale", "total_count", "logits", "probs", "rate",
 201            "concentration", "concentration0", "concentration1", "df"
 202        ]:
 203            if hasattr(fn, attr):
 204                v = getattr(fn, attr)
 205                if torch.is_tensor(v):
 206                    tensors.append((attr, v))
 207        return tensors
 208
 209    def diagnose_nonfinite_sites(self, model, guide, *args, **kwargs):
 210        print("\n[DIAG] Running traced guide+model to locate non-finite site...")
 211
 212        guide_trace = poutine.trace(guide).get_trace(*args, **kwargs)
 213        replayed_model = poutine.replay(model, trace=guide_trace)
 214        model_trace = poutine.trace(replayed_model).get_trace(*args, **kwargs)
 215
 216        def scan_trace(tr, label):
 217            print(f"[DIAG] Scanning {label} trace...")
 218            for name, node in tr.nodes.items():
 219                if node.get("type") != "sample":
 220                    continue
 221
 222                fn = node["fn"]
 223                val = node["value"]
 224
 225                if torch.is_tensor(val) and (not torch.isfinite(val).all().item()):
 226                    print(f"  [BAD VALUE] site={name}")
 227                    self._print_tensor(f"{label}:{name}.value", val, prefix="    ")
 228                    return name
 229
 230                for attr, ten in self._collect_dist_tensors(fn):
 231                    if not torch.isfinite(ten).all().item():
 232                        print(f"  [BAD DIST PARAM] site={name} param={attr}")
 233                        self._print_tensor(f"{label}:{name}.fn.{attr}", ten, prefix="    ")
 234                        return name
 235
 236                if "log_prob" in node:
 237                    lp = node["log_prob"]
 238                    if torch.is_tensor(lp) and (not torch.isfinite(lp).all().item()):
 239                        print(f"  [BAD LOG_PROB] site={name}")
 240                        self._print_tensor(f"{label}:{name}.log_prob", lp, prefix="    ")
 241                        return name
 242
 243            print(f"[DIAG] No non-finite sample sites found in {label} trace.")
 244            return None
 245
 246        bad_guide = scan_trace(guide_trace, "guide")
 247        bad_model = scan_trace(model_trace, "model")
 248        print(f"[DIAG] First bad site guide={bad_guide} model={bad_model}\n")
 249
 250    def _debug_svi_step(self, svi, step, prev_finite, *args, **kwargs):
 251        """
 252        A 'manual' SVI step that lets us check:
 253          - pre-step params
 254          - post-grads, pre-update params/grads
 255          - post-update params
 256        and run trace diagnosis on first failure.
 257        """
 258        # Pre-step check
 259        prev_finite, any_bad = self._check_param_store_all(
 260            step, svi=svi, where="(pre-step)", prev_finite=prev_finite
 261        )
 262        if any_bad:
 263            store = pyro.get_param_store()
 264            if "locs.log_K_a" in store and store["locs.log_K_a"].grad is not None:
 265                g = store["locs.log_K_a"].grad
 266                bad_idx = torch.nonzero(torch.isnan(g), as_tuple=False).squeeze(-1)
 267                if bad_idx.numel() > 0:
 268                    self._diagnose_log_Ka_nan_grad(svi, bad_idx, *args, **kwargs)
 269        
 270            self.diagnose_nonfinite_sites(svi.model, svi.guide, *args, **kwargs)
 271            raise FloatingPointError("Non-finite grads/params after loss_and_grads (before update).")
 272
 273
 274        # Compute loss + grads (no update yet)
 275        with poutine.trace(param_only=True) as param_capture:
 276            loss = svi.loss_and_grads(svi.model, svi.guide, *args, **kwargs)
 277
 278        # Post-grads check (this often catches the real cause)
 279        prev_finite, any_bad = self._check_param_store_all(
 280            step, svi=svi, where="(post-grads, pre-update)", prev_finite=prev_finite
 281        )
 282        if any_bad:
 283            store = pyro.get_param_store()
 284            if "locs.log_K_a" in store and store["locs.log_K_a"].grad is not None:
 285                g = store["locs.log_K_a"].grad
 286                bad_idx = torch.nonzero(torch.isnan(g), as_tuple=False).squeeze(-1)
 287                if bad_idx.numel() > 0:
 288                    self._diagnose_log_Ka_nan_grad(svi, bad_idx, *args, **kwargs)
 289            self.diagnose_nonfinite_sites(svi.model, svi.guide, *args, **kwargs)
 290            # Fitting will stop: FloatingPointError is caught in the main loop → [STOP] + break
 291            raise FloatingPointError("Non-finite grads/params after loss_and_grads (before update).")
 292
 293        # Apply optimizer update
 294        params = set(site["value"].unconstrained() for site in param_capture.trace.nodes.values())
 295        svi.optim(params)
 296
 297        # Post-update check
 298        prev_finite, any_bad = self._check_param_store_all(
 299            step, svi=svi, where="(post-update)", prev_finite=prev_finite
 300        )
 301        if any_bad:
 302            store = pyro.get_param_store()
 303            if "locs.log_K_a" in store and store["locs.log_K_a"].grad is not None:
 304                g = store["locs.log_K_a"].grad
 305                bad_idx = torch.nonzero(torch.isnan(g), as_tuple=False).squeeze(-1)
 306                if bad_idx.numel() > 0:
 307                    self._diagnose_log_Ka_nan_grad(svi, bad_idx, *args, **kwargs)
 308            self.diagnose_nonfinite_sites(svi.model, svi.guide, *args, **kwargs)
 309            # Fitting will stop: FloatingPointError is caught in the main loop → [STOP] + break
 310            raise FloatingPointError("Optimizer update produced non-finite params.")
 311
 312        return loss, prev_finite
 313
 314    def _diagnose_log_Ka_nan_grad(self, svi, bad_idx, *args, **kwargs):
 315        """
 316        bad_idx: 1D LongTensor of indices where locs.log_K_a.grad is NaN
 317        Prints model/guide site values for those indices and derived quantities
 318        (phi, Hill logit range, NB logits range).
 319        """
 320        import pyro.poutine as poutine
 321        import torch
 322    
 323        print(f"\n[DIAG+] NaN grad indices for log_K_a: {bad_idx.tolist()}")
 324    
 325        guide_trace = poutine.trace(svi.guide).get_trace(*args, **kwargs)
 326        replayed_model = poutine.replay(svi.model, trace=guide_trace)
 327        model_trace = poutine.trace(replayed_model).get_trace(*args, **kwargs)
 328    
 329        def get_site(tr, name):
 330            return tr.nodes[name]["value"] if name in tr.nodes else None
 331    
 332        # --- pull site values (all should be finite, but may be extreme) ---
 333        def _first_nonnone(*vals):
 334            return next((v for v in vals if v is not None), None)
 335        log_K_a = _first_nonnone(get_site(model_trace, "log_K_a"), get_site(guide_trace, "log_K_a"))
 336        log_Vmax_a = _first_nonnone(get_site(model_trace, "log_Vmax_a"), get_site(guide_trace, "log_Vmax_a"))
 337        Vmax_a = get_site(model_trace, "Vmax_a")
 338        K_a = get_site(model_trace, "K_a")
 339        n_a = get_site(model_trace, "n_a")
 340        A = get_site(model_trace, "A")
 341        o_y = get_site(model_trace, "o_y")  # sampled per feature
 342        alpha = get_site(model_trace, "alpha")  # relaxed bernoulli
 343    
 344        # Some of these might not exist depending on branch / naming
 345        for name, tensor in [
 346            ("log_K_a", log_K_a),
 347            ("K_a", K_a),
 348            ("log_Vmax_a", log_Vmax_a),
 349            ("Vmax_a", Vmax_a),
 350            ("n_a", n_a),
 351            ("A", A),
 352            ("o_y", o_y),
 353            ("alpha", alpha),
 354        ]:
 355            if tensor is None:
 356                continue
 357            sel = tensor[bad_idx]
 358            self._print_tensor(f"{name}[bad_idx]", sel, prefix="  ")
 359    
 360        # --- derived phi and ranges (very informative) ---
 361        if o_y is not None:
 362            phi = 1.0 / (o_y ** 2)
 363            self._print_tensor("phi_y[bad_idx]", phi[bad_idx], prefix="  ")
 364    
 365        # --- derived Hill logit range (this catches x**n instabilities) ---
 366        # kwargs must include x_true_sample, and we prefer to use log_K_a directly
 367        x_true = kwargs.get("x_true_sample", None)
 368        if x_true is not None and log_K_a is not None and n_a is not None:
 369            tiny = torch.finfo(x_true.dtype).tiny
 370            log_x = torch.log(x_true.clamp_min(tiny)).unsqueeze(-1)  # [N,1]
 371            # logit for each bad feature: [N, |bad_idx|]
 372            logit = (n_a[bad_idx].unsqueeze(0) * (log_x - log_K_a[bad_idx].unsqueeze(0)))
 373            # print range across cells (per bad feature)
 374            logit_min = logit.min(dim=0).values
 375            logit_max = logit.max(dim=0).values
 376            self._print_tensor("hill_logit_min[bad_idx]", logit_min, prefix="  ")
 377            self._print_tensor("hill_logit_max[bad_idx]", logit_max, prefix="  ")
 378    
 379            # approximate Hill output range
 380            if Vmax_a is not None:
 381                H = Vmax_a[bad_idx].unsqueeze(0) * torch.sigmoid(logit)
 382                self._print_tensor("Hilla_min[bad_idx]", H.min(dim=0).values, prefix="  ")
 383                self._print_tensor("Hilla_max[bad_idx]", H.max(dim=0).values, prefix="  ")
 384    
 385        # --- derived NB logits range for bad features (if you pass mu_y pieces) ---
 386        # We can’t see mu_final unless you expose it; but we can at least compute the part driven by Hill:
 387        # If you want full mu_final, expose it via pyro.deterministic (recommended).
 388        print("[DIAG+] If hill_logit range is extreme (e.g. > ~80 in magnitude), Hill math/backward is a prime suspect.\n")
 389
 390    
 391    #########################################
 392    ## Step 3: Fit trans effects (model_y) ##
 393    #########################################
 394    def _model_y(
 395        self,
 396        N,
 397        T,
 398        y_obs_tensor,
 399        sum_factor_tensor,
 400        beta_o_alpha_tensor,
 401        beta_o_beta_tensor,
 402        K_max_tensor,
 403        K_alpha_tensor,
 404        Vmax_mean_tensor,
 405        Vmax_alpha_tensor,
 406        n_mu_tensor,
 407        Amean_tensor,
 408        p_n_logits_tensor,
 409        epsilon_tensor,
 410        x_true_sample,
 411        nmin,
 412        nmax,
 413        alpha_y_sample=None,
 414        C=None,
 415        groups_tensor=None,
 416        temperature=1.0,
 417        use_straight_through=False,
 418        function_type='single_hill',
 419        polynomial_degree=6,
 420        use_alpha=True,
 421        distribution='negbinom',
 422        denominator_tensor=None,
 423        K=None,
 424        x_true_CV=None,
 425        x_ntc_mean=None,
 426        use_epsilon=True,
 427        vmax_log_sigma_floor_tensor=None,
 428        k_log_sigma_min_tensor=None,
 429        k_center_tensor=None,
 430        y_ntc_tensor=None,
 431        mean_y_corrected_tensor=None,
 432        o_y_ntc_tensor=None,
 433        sigma_hat_tensor=None,
 434        alpha_n_coupling: float = 10.0,
 435        latents_only=False,
 436    ):
 437
 438        if use_alpha:
 439            alpha_dist = dist.RelaxedBernoulliStraightThrough if use_straight_through else dist.RelaxedBernoulli
 440
 441        trans_plate = pyro.plate("trans_plate", T, dim=-1)
 442        
 443        ##########
 444        ## x_true (Now Fully Observed) ##
 445        ##########
 446        x_true = x_true_sample
 447    
 448        ####################
 449        ## alpha_y ##
 450        ####################
 451        alpha_y = None
 452        if alpha_y_sample is not None:
 453            alpha_y = alpha_y_sample
 454    
 455        ##############################################
 456        ## Feature-level variance (distribution-specific)
 457        ##############################################
 458        phi_y_used = None  # NB dispersion; None for other distributions
 459        sigma_y    = None  # noise scale for normal/studentt
 460
 461        if distribution == 'negbinom':
 462            beta_o = pyro.sample("beta_o", dist.Gamma(beta_o_alpha_tensor, beta_o_beta_tensor))
 463            with trans_plate:
 464                o_y = pyro.sample("o_y", dist.Exponential(beta_o))
 465                phi_y = 1 / (o_y**2)
 466            phi_y_used = phi_y.unsqueeze(-2)
 467            # A-prior weight: noisier genes get stronger pull toward NTC anchor.
 468            # Use NTC-estimated o_y when available (sampled o_y is near-unidentifiable
 469            # in fit_trans, so its posterior stays close to the prior mean for all genes).
 470            _prior_mean_o_y = (beta_o_beta_tensor / beta_o_alpha_tensor).clamp_min(epsilon_tensor)
 471            if o_y_ntc_tensor is not None:
 472                _o_y_weight = o_y_ntc_tensor / (o_y_ntc_tensor + _prior_mean_o_y)  # [T], fixed
 473            else:
 474                _o_y_weight = o_y / (o_y + _prior_mean_o_y)  # [T], sampled (fallback)
 475
 476        elif distribution in ('normal', 'studentt'):
 477            with trans_plate:
 478                if sigma_hat_tensor is not None:
 479                    sigma_y = pyro.sample("sigma_y", dist.HalfNormal(2.0 * sigma_hat_tensor))
 480                    # A-prior weight: features with larger NTC sigma pulled more toward NTC anchor.
 481                    _sigma_ref = sigma_hat_tensor.mean().clamp_min(epsilon_tensor)
 482                    _o_y_weight = sigma_hat_tensor / (sigma_hat_tensor + _sigma_ref)  # [T], fixed
 483                else:
 484                    sigma_y = pyro.sample("sigma_y", dist.HalfCauchy(self._t(10.0)))
 485                    _o_y_weight = self._t(0.5)  # neutral without NTC data
 486
 487        else:  # binomial, multinomial — variance fully determined by count totals
 488            _o_y_weight = self._t(0.5)  # neutral; no per-feature noise parameter
 489
 490        # Degrees of freedom: Student-t only, fixed at 3 to match fit_ntc
 491        nu_y = self._t(3.0) if distribution == 'studentt' else None
 492    
 493        #################
 494        ## Hill-based: ##
 495        #################
 496        if function_type in ['polynomial']:
 497            #sigma_coeff = pyro.sample("sigma_coeff", dist.Exponential(100)) #   -> controls how variable n_a can be across genes
 498            sigma_coeff = pyro.sample("sigma_coeff", dist.HalfCauchy(scale=self._t(1.0)))
 499        
 500        # Now enter the trans_plate (T dimension)
 501        with trans_plate:
 502
 503            # For multinomial, Amean_tensor and Vmax_mean_tensor are already [T, K] shaped
 504            # For binomial, they are [T] shaped
 505            # We keep them in their native shape for per-category priors in multinomial
 506
 507            # Baseline parameter A depends on distribution:
 508            # - normal/studentt: can be negative (natural value space)
 509            # - negbinom: positive count
 510            # - binomial/multinomial: probability in [0,1], using NEW reparameterization
 511            if distribution in ['normal', 'studentt']:
 512                # A prior: NTC-anchored Normal (analogous to negbinom LogNormal, but in linear
 513                # space since normal/studentt values can be negative).
 514                #
 515                # When y_ntc available (fit_ntc has been run):
 516                #   w → 0 (quiet feature): prior centred at Amean; y_ntc is 1σ above
 517                #   w → 1 (noisy feature): prior centred at y_ntc
 518                #   sigma = |y_ntc − Amean| floored at 10% of response amplitude
 519                #
 520                # Fallback (no NTC posterior): fixed-shift approach using response amplitude.
 521                delta_A = (Vmax_mean_tensor - Amean_tensor).clamp_min(epsilon_tensor)
 522                if y_ntc_tensor is not None:
 523                    sigma_A = (y_ntc_tensor - Amean_tensor).abs().clamp_min(delta_A * 0.1)
 524                    mean_A  = (1.0 - _o_y_weight) * Amean_tensor + _o_y_weight * y_ntc_tensor
 525                else:
 526                    sigma_A = delta_A
 527                    _shift_A = (1.0 - _o_y_weight) * 0.55
 528                    mean_A  = Amean_tensor - _shift_A * delta_A
 529                A = pyro.sample("A", dist.Normal(mean_A, sigma_A))
 530
 531            elif distribution in ['binomial', 'multinomial']:
 532                # Beta/Dirichlet priors for bounded [0, 1] likelihoods.
 533                # For binomial:    A ~ Beta(1, β) with mean = 0.5×Q05
 534                # For multinomial: A ~ Dirichlet with mean = 0.5×Q05 (row-normalized)
 535                #
 536                # POTENTIAL IMPROVEMENT: noise-adaptive shift (not yet implemented).
 537                # Analogous to the o_y weighting for negbinom/normal/studentt, the A prior
 538                # shift could be attenuated for low-coverage features where PSI estimates
 539                # are unreliable. The natural noise proxy is mean denominator read depth:
 540                #   _binom_weight = n_ref / (n_ref + mean_denom)   ∈ (0, 1)
 541                #   shift = 0.5 * (1 - _binom_weight)              (0.5 → 0 as reads increase)
 542                # where mean_denom = obs_denom.mean(cells) for binomial, or
 543                # obs_counts.sum(categories).mean(cells) for multinomial.
 544                # A data-adaptive n_ref = median(mean_denom) across features would be
 545                # more principled than a fixed count threshold.
 546
 547                # Amean_tensor: [T] for binomial, [T, K] for multinomial
 548                # Vmax_mean_tensor: [T] for binomial, [T, K] for multinomial
 549
 550                # Sample A
 551                if distribution == 'multinomial' and Amean_tensor.ndim > 1:
 552                    # For multinomial: LogisticNormal prior on A (Normal in logit space + softmax).
 553                    #
 554                    # We previously used dist.Dirichlet, but Pyro's autoguide represents the
 555                    # K-simplex via a stick-breaking transform from R^(K-1).  With K=65 and
 556                    # many phantom (all-zero) categories, float32 rounding in the stick-breaking
 557                    # product chain makes the sample sum drift away from 1.0 beyond PyTorch's
 558                    # 1e-6 Simplex tolerance, raising a ValueError in both compute_log_prob and
 559                    # compute_score_parts — even with validate_args=False on the model, the
 560                    # guide's TransformedDistribution re-validates the same sample.
 561                    #
 562                    # LogisticNormal sidesteps this entirely: the guide uses an unconstrained
 563                    # Normal site (no simplex constraint, no stick-breaking), and softmax
 564                    # guarantees a valid probability vector in the model.
 565                    K_dim = Amean_tensor.shape[-1]
 566
 567                    # Build phantom mask (categories with zero observations across all cells)
 568                    phantom_conc_mask = None
 569                    if y_obs_tensor.dim() == 3:  # multinomial: [N, T, K]
 570                        obs_total = y_obs_tensor.sum(dim=0)  # [T, K]
 571                        phantom_conc_mask = (obs_total == 0)  # [T, K]
 572
 573                    # Logit-space prior mean (base: from Q05)
 574                    A_mean_clamped = (0.5 * Amean_tensor).clamp(min=epsilon_tensor, max=1.0 - epsilon_tensor)
 575                    A_mean_normalized = A_mean_clamped / A_mean_clamped.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)  # [T, K]
 576                    A_logit_mean_base = torch.log(A_mean_normalized.clamp(min=1e-10))              # [T, K]
 577
 578                    # A prior: w-interpolated LogisticNormal anchored between data-driven
 579                    # lower anchor and y_ntc. Mode at (1-w)*A_logit_mean_base + w*logit(y_ntc),
 580                    # where w = o_y_ntc / (o_y_ntc + prior_mean_o_y).
 581                    if y_ntc_tensor is not None:
 582                        if y_ntc_tensor.ndim != 2 or y_ntc_tensor.shape[0] != T or y_ntc_tensor.shape[1] != K_dim:
 583                            raise ValueError(
 584                                f"y_ntc_tensor shape {tuple(y_ntc_tensor.shape)} does not match "
 585                                f"expected multinomial shape [{T}, {K_dim}]."
 586                            )
 587                        logit_y_ntc       = torch.log(y_ntc_tensor.clamp(min=1e-10))      # [T, K], log-simplex
 588                        A_logit_mean_base = torch.maximum(A_logit_mean_base, logit_y_ntc - 4.0)
 589                        w_expanded        = _o_y_weight.unsqueeze(-1)                      # [T, 1]
 590                        A_logit_mean      = (1.0 - w_expanded) * A_logit_mean_base + w_expanded * logit_y_ntc  # [T, K]
 591                        sigma_A_logit     = (logit_y_ntc - A_logit_mean_base).abs().clamp_min(1.0)             # [T, K]
 592                    else:
 593                        A_logit_mean  = A_logit_mean_base
 594                        sigma_A_logit = self._t(1.0)
 595
 596                    # Push phantom categories to -inf in prior mean so the guide learns
 597                    # to assign them zero probability.
 598                    if phantom_conc_mask is not None:
 599                        A_logit_mean = A_logit_mean.masked_fill(phantom_conc_mask, -1e4)
 600
 601                    # Sample in unconstrained logit space — no simplex constraint, no stick-breaking.
 602                    A_logit = pyro.sample("A", dist.Normal(A_logit_mean, sigma_A_logit).to_event(1))  # [T, K]
 603
 604                    # Softmax with phantom masking → valid probability vector [T, K]
 605                    if phantom_conc_mask is not None:
 606                        A_logit = A_logit.masked_fill(phantom_conc_mask, -1e9)
 607                    A = torch.softmax(A_logit, dim=-1)  # [T, K]
 608
 609                else:
 610                    # For binomial: Logit-Normal prior when y_ntc available (analogous to negbinom
 611                    # LogNormal, adapted to the [0,1] simplex via logit transform).
 612                    #
 613                    # When y_ntc available:
 614                    #   Lower anchor: logit(Amean/2); upper anchor: logit(y_ntc)
 615                    #   w → 0 (quiet feature): centred at logit(Amean/2); y_ntc is 1σ above
 616                    #   w → 1 (noisy feature): centred at logit(y_ntc)
 617                    #   sigma = (logit(y_ntc) − logit(Amean/2)).clamp_min(1 logit unit)
 618                    #
 619                    # Fallback (no NTC posterior): Beta(1, β) with mean = 0.5×Q05.
 620                    if y_ntc_tensor is not None:
 621                        # Lift upper anchor to mean(y_corrected) when y_ntc < mean.
 622                        if mean_y_corrected_tensor is not None:
 623                            effective_y_ntc = torch.maximum(y_ntc_tensor, mean_y_corrected_tensor)
 624                        else:
 625                            effective_y_ntc = y_ntc_tensor
 626                        logit_Amean_half = torch.logit((0.5 * Amean_tensor).clamp(1e-6, 1.0 - 1e-6))      # [T]
 627                        logit_y_ntc      = torch.logit(effective_y_ntc.clamp(1e-6, 1.0 - 1e-6))            # [T]
 628                        logit_Amean_half = torch.maximum(logit_Amean_half, logit_y_ntc - 4.0)              # cap: sigma ≤ 4
 629                        sigma_logit = (logit_y_ntc - logit_Amean_half).clamp_min(1.0)                      # [T]
 630                        mu_logit    = (1.0 - _o_y_weight) * logit_Amean_half + _o_y_weight * logit_y_ntc  # [T]
 631                        logit_A = pyro.sample("logit_A", dist.Normal(mu_logit, sigma_logit))            # [T]
 632                        A = pyro.deterministic("A", torch.sigmoid(logit_A))                             # [T]
 633                    else:
 634                        A_mean_shifted = (0.5 * Amean_tensor).clamp_min(epsilon_tensor)
 635                        beta_A = (1.0 - A_mean_shifted) / A_mean_shifted                               # [T]
 636                        A = pyro.sample("A", dist.Beta(self._t(1.0), beta_A).expand([T]))              # [T]
 637
 638            else:
 639                # For negbinom: LogNormal A prior (Normal in log2 space) with noise-adaptive mean.
 640                # log2(A) ~ Normal(mu_log2_A, sigma_log2_A), so A = 2^log2(A).
 641                #
 642                # mu_log2_A interpolates in log2 space between two gene-specific anchors:
 643                #   w → 0 (quiet gene, informative likelihood): log2(Amean/2)
 644                #   w → 1 (noisy gene, weak likelihood):        log2(y_ntc)
 645                #
 646                # sigma_log2_A = log2(y_ntc) - lower_anchor, floored at 1 octave, capped at 4.
 647                if y_ntc_tensor is not None:
 648                    log2_y_ntc = torch.log2(y_ntc_tensor)
 649                    # Lift upper anchor to mean(y_corrected) when y_ntc < mean — prevents
 650                    # both anchors collapsing to the floor for genes absent in NTC but
 651                    # expressed in perturbed conditions.
 652                    if mean_y_corrected_tensor is not None:
 653                        log2_upper_anchor = torch.maximum(log2_y_ntc, torch.log2(mean_y_corrected_tensor))
 654                    else:
 655                        log2_upper_anchor = log2_y_ntc
 656                    log2_Amean_half = torch.maximum(
 657                        torch.log2(Amean_tensor / 2.0),
 658                        log2_upper_anchor - 4.0,
 659                    )
 660                    sigma_log2_A = (log2_upper_anchor - log2_Amean_half).clamp_min(1.0)  # ≤ 4 octaves
 661                    mu_log2_A    = (1.0 - _o_y_weight) * log2_Amean_half + _o_y_weight * log2_upper_anchor
 662                else:
 663                    log2_Amean_half = torch.log2(Amean_tensor / 2.0)
 664                    sigma_log2_A    = self._t(4.0)
 665                    mu_log2_A       = log2_Amean_half
 666                log2_A = pyro.sample("log2_A", dist.Normal(mu_log2_A, sigma_log2_A))
 667                A = pyro.deterministic("A", torch.pow(self._t(2.0), log2_A))
 668
 669            if use_alpha:
 670                # Relaxed Bernoulli: alpha ~ (0,1), becomes more discrete as temperature -> 0
 671                # For multinomial: per-category gate — each of the K-1 categories can
 672                # independently be "on" or "off". This allows, e.g., only one acceptor to
 673                # respond while others remain flat. The Kth (residual) category is affected
 674                # iff at least one K-1 category is on (conservation of probability).
 675                if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 676                    alpha = pyro.sample("alpha", alpha_dist(temperature=temperature, logits=p_n_logits_tensor).expand([K - 1]).to_event(1))  # [T, K-1]
 677                else:
 678                    alpha = pyro.sample("alpha", alpha_dist(temperature=temperature, logits=p_n_logits_tensor))  # [T]
 679            else:
 680                if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 681                    alpha = torch.ones((T, K - 1), device=self.model.device)
 682                else:
 683                    alpha = torch.ones((T,), device=self.model.device)
 684            
 685            if function_type in ['single_hill', 'additive_hill', 'nested_hill']:
 686
 687                #####################################
 688                ## function priors (depend on o_y) ##
 689                #####################################
 690                # Gamma and delta depend on T dimension
 691                # Reduce over group dimension if necessary
 692                K_sigma = (K_max_tensor / (self._t(2) * torch.sqrt(K_alpha_tensor))) + epsilon_tensor
 693
 694                # For multinomial, reduce [T, K] → [T] for the Hill function amplitude prior
 695                # For other distributions, use Vmax_mean_tensor directly
 696                if distribution == 'multinomial' and Vmax_mean_tensor.ndim > 1:
 697                    Vmax_prior_mean = Vmax_mean_tensor.mean(dim=-1)  # [T]
 698                else:
 699                    Vmax_prior_mean = Vmax_mean_tensor  # [T]
 700
 701                Vmax_sigma = (Vmax_prior_mean / torch.sqrt(Vmax_alpha_tensor)) + epsilon_tensor
 702
 703                # Compute the unconstrained prior mean for n_raw that maps to n_mu under
 704                # soft_clamp.  Without this correction, Normal(0, sigma) on n_raw has its
 705                # constrained mode at center_n = (nmin + nmax)/2, which can be far from 0
 706                # when nmin/nmax are asymmetric (e.g. all x > 1 → nmin = −100, center ≈ −31).
 707                _center_n = 0.5 * (nmax + nmin)
 708                _half_n   = 0.5 * (nmax - nmin).clamp_min(epsilon_tensor)
 709                _ratio_n  = ((n_mu_tensor - _center_n) / _half_n).clamp(-1 + 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6)
 710                n_mu_raw_tensor = _half_n * torch.atanh(_ratio_n)
 711
 712                # Per-gene n scale: sampled inside trans_plate so each gene is
 713                # independently regularised (prevents one noisy gene from inflating
 714                # the global sigma and loosening the prior for all other genes).
 715                sigma_n_a = pyro.sample("sigma_n_a", dist.Exponential(self._t(1.0)))
 716
 717                # For multinomial, we need per-category parameters (K-1 categories, Kth is residual)
 718                if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 719                    K_minus_1 = K - 1
 720                    # Sample parameters for K-1 categories
 721                    # Each category gets its own Hill function parameters
 722                    # Use .to_event(1) instead of a nested plate to avoid dim=-1 collision with trans_plate
 723                    n_a_raw = pyro.sample("n_a_raw", dist.Normal(n_mu_raw_tensor, sigma_n_a.unsqueeze(-1).expand(T, K_minus_1)).to_event(1))  # [T, K-1]
 724                    n_a = pyro.deterministic(
 725                        "n_a",
 726                        _soft_clamp(n_a_raw, nmin, nmax)
 727                    )  # [T, K-1]
 728                else:
 729                    # For non-multinomial: single set of parameters per feature
 730                    n_a_raw = pyro.sample("n_a_raw", dist.Normal(n_mu_raw_tensor, sigma_n_a))
 731                    n_a = pyro.deterministic(
 732                        "n_a",
 733                        _soft_clamp(n_a_raw, nmin, nmax)
 734                    )
 735
 736                # Identifiability coupling: when n_a≈0 the Hill is flat and alpha·Vmax is
 737                # just a constant offset, indistinguishable from A.  Penalise alpha by
 738                # exp(-|n_a|): coupling=1 at n=0, 0.37 at n=1, 0.14 at n=2.
 739                # This keeps alpha near 0 until the data pushes n_a away from 0.
 740                if use_alpha and alpha_n_coupling > 0.0:
 741                    _flatness_a = torch.exp(-torch.abs(n_a))  # [T] or [T, K-1]
 742                    if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 743                        pyro.factor("alpha_n_coupling_a", -(alpha * _flatness_a * alpha_n_coupling).sum(dim=-1))
 744                    else:
 745                        pyro.factor("alpha_n_coupling_a", -(alpha * _flatness_a * alpha_n_coupling))
 746
 747                # Scale for Vmax, K is multiplied by alpha
 748                #eff_Vmax_sigma = alpha * Vmaxa_sigma + epsilon_tensor
 749                #eff_Ka_sigma   = alpha * Ka_sigma    + epsilon_tensor
 750
 751                # UNIFIED Vmax and K priors (Log-Normal for all distributions)
 752                # K uses CV-based std (scale-invariant, works without guides)
 753                # Vmax uses raw variance (data-driven) for negbinom/normal/studentt
 754
 755                # K parameterization (UNIFIED for all distributions)
 756                # When NTC mean is known, center the prior there with ±5 log2FC coverage.
 757                # This ensures the P.O.I. starts within the observed x-range regardless of
 758                # whether the subset is KO-only, CA-only, or full.
 759                #
 760                # Minimum prior width: K_log_sigma >= 5*ln(2)/2 ≈ 1.73
 761                # This guarantees the lower end of the 95% CI extends at least 2^{-5} (1/32x)
 762                # below the prior centre, matching the NTC-centred branch below.
 763                _K_log_sigma_min = (k_log_sigma_min_tensor
 764                                    if k_log_sigma_min_tensor is not None
 765                                    else self._t(5.0 * 0.6931 / 2.0))
 766
 767                if x_ntc_mean is not None:
 768                    # K prior: log-normal with MEDIAN at x_ntc_mean (= log2FC 0).
 769                    # In log2FC space: log2(K_a) ~ Normal(0, sigma_log2²) where
 770                    # sigma_log2 = K_log_sigma / ln(2) = 2.5, giving a 95% CI of ±5 log2FC.
 771                    # Setting K_log_mu = log(x_ntc_mean) centres the median (not the mean)
 772                    # at NTC, which is the natural reference in log2FC space.
 773                    K_log_sigma = _K_log_sigma_min  # = 5*ln(2)/2 → sigma_log2 = 2.5
 774                    K_log_mu = torch.log(x_ntc_mean.clamp_min(epsilon_tensor))
 775                else:
 776                    # Fallback: centre median at user-specified quantile of x_true (k_prior_center).
 777                    # Default: middle of observed range (K_max/2). Width from CV.
 778                    # Floor sigma so the prior always spans at least ±5 log2FC.
 779                    _k_fallback = (k_center_tensor if k_center_tensor is not None
 780                                   else K_max_tensor / 2.0)
 781                    K_mean_prior = _k_fallback.clamp_min(epsilon_tensor)
 782                    if x_true_CV is not None:
 783                        K_std_prior = K_mean_prior * x_true_CV
 784                    else:
 785                        K_std_prior = K_max_tensor / (self._t(2.0) * torch.sqrt(K_alpha_tensor))
 786                    ratio_K = (K_std_prior / K_mean_prior).clamp_min(self._t(1e-6))
 787                    K_log_sigma = torch.sqrt(torch.log1p(ratio_K ** 2)).clamp_min(_K_log_sigma_min)
 788                    K_log_mu = torch.log(K_mean_prior)
 789
 790                if distribution in ['binomial', 'multinomial']:
 791                    # For binomial/multinomial: Sample Vmax_a INDEPENDENTLY (like BCD1C4F)
 792                    # Even for multinomial, the Kth category is residual, so we can have independent Vmax
 793                    # This gives Vmax_a direct gradient signal, not mediated through alpha
 794                    # Avoids chicken-and-egg: alpha needs signal → signal needs Vmax → Vmax needs alpha
 795                    Vmax_mean_clamped = Vmax_mean_tensor.clamp(min=0.01, max=0.99)
 796                    # concentration=2 gives CV ≈ 0.6-1.0 depending on the mean —
 797                    # much more diffuse than the previous 10, allowing the posterior
 798                    # to explore Vmax values well above the data-driven estimate when
 799                    # only part of the dose-response range is observed.
 800                    concentration_vmax = self._t(2.0)
 801                    alpha_vmax = Vmax_mean_clamped * concentration_vmax
 802                    beta_vmax = (1 - Vmax_mean_clamped) * concentration_vmax
 803
 804                    if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 805                        # For multinomial: Sample Vmax_a for K-1 categories (Kth is residual)
 806                        # Use .to_event(1) instead of nested plates to avoid dim=-1 collision with trans_plate
 807                        K_minus_1 = K - 1
 808                        Vmax_a = pyro.sample("Vmax_a", dist.Beta(alpha_vmax[:, :K_minus_1], beta_vmax[:, :K_minus_1]).to_event(1))  # [T, K-1]
 809
 810                        # K_a: Log-Normal for K-1 categories
 811                        log_K_a = pyro.sample("log_K_a", dist.Normal(K_log_mu, K_log_sigma).expand([K_minus_1]).to_event(1))  # [T, K-1]
 812                        K_a = pyro.deterministic("K_a", torch.exp(log_K_a))  # [T, K-1]
 813                    else:
 814                        # For binomial: per-feature Vmax_a and K_a
 815                        Vmax_a = pyro.sample("Vmax_a", dist.Beta(alpha_vmax, beta_vmax))  # [T]
 816                        log_K_a = pyro.sample("log_K_a", dist.Normal(K_log_mu, K_log_sigma))  # [T]
 817                        K_a = pyro.deterministic("K_a", torch.exp(log_K_a))  # [T]
 818
 819                else:
 820                    # Vmax prior: LogNormal for negbinom, normal, and studentt alike.
 821                    # Direction of effect is carried by n (negative n = repressor Hill),
 822                    # so Vmax must be strictly positive for all three distributions.
 823                    # Wide log_sigma (floor ≥ 1.5, ≈ 20× range) keeps the prior diffuse
 824                    # enough for one-sided subsets (single technical group).
 825                    _Vmax_log_sigma_floor = (vmax_log_sigma_floor_tensor
 826                                             if vmax_log_sigma_floor_tensor is not None
 827                                             else self._t(1.5))
 828                    Vmax_sigma = (Vmax_prior_mean / torch.sqrt(Vmax_alpha_tensor)) + epsilon_tensor
 829                    Vmax_log_sigma = torch.sqrt(
 830                        torch.log1p((Vmax_sigma / Vmax_prior_mean) ** 2)
 831                    ).clamp_min(_Vmax_log_sigma_floor)
 832                    Vmax_log_mu = (torch.log(Vmax_prior_mean.clamp_min(epsilon_tensor))
 833                                   - 0.5 * Vmax_log_sigma ** 2)
 834                    log_Vmax_a = pyro.sample("log_Vmax_a", dist.Normal(Vmax_log_mu, Vmax_log_sigma))
 835                    Vmax_a = pyro.deterministic("Vmax_a", torch.exp(log_Vmax_a))
 836
 837                    log_K_a = pyro.sample("log_K_a", dist.Normal(K_log_mu, K_log_sigma))
 838                    K_a = pyro.deterministic("K_a", torch.exp(log_K_a))
 839
 840                # Sample all required parameters (additive_hill and nested_hill need second set)
 841                if function_type in ['additive_hill', 'nested_hill']:
 842                    sigma_n_b = pyro.sample("sigma_n_b", dist.Exponential(self._t(1.0)))
 843                    if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 844                        # Use .to_event(1) instead of nested plate to avoid dim=-1 collision with trans_plate
 845                        beta = pyro.sample("beta", alpha_dist(temperature=temperature, logits=p_n_logits_tensor).expand([K - 1]).to_event(1))  # [T, K-1]
 846                    else:
 847                        beta = pyro.sample("beta", alpha_dist(temperature=temperature, logits=p_n_logits_tensor))  # [T]
 848
 849                    # n_b: per-category for multinomial, single for others
 850                    if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 851                        # Use .to_event(1) instead of nested plate to avoid dim=-1 collision with trans_plate
 852                        K_minus_1 = K - 1
 853                        n_b_raw = pyro.sample("n_b_raw", dist.Normal(n_mu_raw_tensor, sigma_n_b.unsqueeze(-1).expand(T, K_minus_1)).to_event(1))  # [T, K-1]
 854                        n_b = pyro.deterministic(
 855                            "n_b",
 856                            _soft_clamp(n_b_raw, nmin, nmax)
 857                        )  # [T, K-1]
 858                    else:
 859                        n_b_raw = pyro.sample("n_b_raw", dist.Normal(n_mu_raw_tensor, sigma_n_b))
 860                        n_b = pyro.deterministic(
 861                            "n_b",
 862                            _soft_clamp(n_b_raw, nmin, nmax)
 863                        )
 864
 865                    # Identifiability coupling for beta/n_b (same logic as alpha/n_a above).
 866                    if use_alpha and alpha_n_coupling > 0.0:
 867                        _flatness_b = torch.exp(-torch.abs(n_b))  # [T] or [T, K-1]
 868                        if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 869                            pyro.factor("alpha_n_coupling_b", -(beta * _flatness_b * alpha_n_coupling).sum(dim=-1))
 870                        else:
 871                            pyro.factor("alpha_n_coupling_b", -(beta * _flatness_b * alpha_n_coupling))
 872
 873                    # Vmax_b and K_b: same structure as Vmax_a and K_a
 874                    if distribution in ['binomial', 'multinomial']:
 875                        if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 876                            # For multinomial: Sample Vmax_b for K-1 categories (Kth is residual)
 877                            # Use .to_event(1) instead of nested plates to avoid dim=-1 collision with trans_plate
 878                            K_minus_1 = K - 1
 879                            Vmax_b = pyro.sample("Vmax_b", dist.Beta(alpha_vmax[:, :K_minus_1], beta_vmax[:, :K_minus_1]).to_event(1))  # [T, K-1]
 880
 881                            # K_b: Log-Normal for K-1 categories
 882                            log_K_b = pyro.sample("log_K_b", dist.Normal(K_log_mu, K_log_sigma).expand([K_minus_1]).to_event(1))  # [T, K-1]
 883                            K_b = pyro.deterministic("K_b", torch.exp(log_K_b))  # [T, K-1]
 884                        else:
 885                            # For binomial: per-feature Vmax_b and K_b
 886                            Vmax_b = pyro.sample("Vmax_b", dist.Beta(alpha_vmax, beta_vmax))  # [T]
 887                            log_K_b = pyro.sample("log_K_b", dist.Normal(K_log_mu, K_log_sigma))  # [T]
 888                            K_b = pyro.deterministic("K_b", torch.exp(log_K_b))  # [T]
 889
 890                    else:
 891                        # Vmax_b: same LogNormal prior as Vmax_a (parameters computed above).
 892                        log_Vmax_b = pyro.sample("log_Vmax_b", dist.Normal(Vmax_log_mu, Vmax_log_sigma))
 893                        Vmax_b = pyro.deterministic("Vmax_b", torch.exp(log_Vmax_b))
 894
 895                        log_K_b = pyro.sample("log_K_b", dist.Normal(K_log_mu, K_log_sigma))
 896                        K_b = pyro.deterministic("K_b", torch.exp(log_K_b))
 897                
 898                # Early exit for memory-efficient posterior sampling.
 899                # All gene-level latent variables (A, alpha, beta, Vmax_a/b, K_a/b, n_a/b,
 900                # o_y, sigma_n_a/b) have been sampled above as [T]-shaped tensors.
 901                # Skipping the cell-level Hill computation avoids creating [N, T] tensors
 902                # (each ~2.68 GB for N=29318, T=22834), which is the source of OOM during
 903                # pyro.infer.Predictive with num_samples > 1.
 904                if latents_only:
 905                    return
 906
 907                # Compute Hill function(s)
 908                # Hill_based_positive returns values in [0, Vmax]
 909                # We compute: y = A + alpha * Hill + beta * Hill (for additive)
 910
 911                if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
 912                    # NEW FORMULATION for multinomial (matching binomial structure):
 913                    # Sample A from Dirichlet (sum to 1)
 914                    # Sample Vmax_a and Vmax_b INDEPENDENTLY for K-1 categories (Kth is residual)
 915                    # For each category k in K-1:
 916                    #   y_k = A_k + (alpha * Hill_a_k(Vmax=Vmax_a_k)) + (beta * Hill_b_k(Vmax=Vmax_b_k))
 917                    # Then: y_K = 1 - sum(y_1, ..., y_{K-1})
 918                    # This ensures probabilities sum to 1, and Kth category gets whatever is left
 919
 920                    K_dim = K
 921                    K_minus_1 = K - 1
 922                    # x_3d: [N, 1, 1] broadcasts over [1, T, K-1] parameter tensors
 923                    x_3d = x_true.unsqueeze(1).unsqueeze(2)  # [N, 1, 1]
 924
 925                    # A is [T, K] from Dirichlet
 926                    # Extract K-1 for fitting Hills (Kth doesn't get a Hill function)
 927                    A_kminus1 = A[..., :K_minus_1]  # [T, K-1]
 928
 929                    # Expand for broadcasting
 930                    A_kminus1_expanded = A_kminus1.unsqueeze(0)  # [1, T, K-1]
 931
 932                    if function_type == 'single_hill':
 933                        # Vectorized over K-1: Vmax_a/log_K_a/n_a all [T, K-1]
 934                        Hilla_kminus1 = Hill_based_positive_logK(
 935                            x_3d, Vmax=Vmax_a.unsqueeze(0), A=0,
 936                            logK=log_K_a.unsqueeze(0), n=n_a.unsqueeze(0)
 937                        )  # [N, T, K-1]
 938                        combined_hill = alpha.unsqueeze(0) * Hilla_kminus1  # [N, T, K-1]
 939                        y_kminus1 = A_kminus1_expanded + combined_hill      # [N, T, K-1]
 940
 941                    elif function_type == 'additive_hill':
 942                        # Vectorized over K-1 for both Hill_a and Hill_b
 943                        Hilla_kminus1 = Hill_based_positive_logK(
 944                            x_3d, Vmax=Vmax_a.unsqueeze(0), A=0,
 945                            logK=log_K_a.unsqueeze(0), n=n_a.unsqueeze(0)
 946                        )  # [N, T, K-1]
 947                        Hillb_kminus1 = Hill_based_positive_logK(
 948                            x_3d, Vmax=Vmax_b.unsqueeze(0), A=0,
 949                            logK=log_K_b.unsqueeze(0), n=n_b.unsqueeze(0)
 950                        )  # [N, T, K-1]
 951                        combined_hill = (alpha.unsqueeze(0) * Hilla_kminus1 +
 952                                         beta.unsqueeze(0) * Hillb_kminus1)  # [N, T, K-1]
 953                        y_kminus1 = A_kminus1_expanded + combined_hill         # [N, T, K-1]
 954
 955                    elif function_type == 'nested_hill':
 956                        # First Hill vectorized over K-1; its output feeds the second Hill
 957                        Hilla_kminus1 = Hill_based_positive_logK(
 958                            x_3d, Vmax=Vmax_a.unsqueeze(0), A=0,
 959                            logK=log_K_a.unsqueeze(0), n=n_a.unsqueeze(0)
 960                        )  # [N, T, K-1]
 961                        Hillb_kminus1 = Hill_based_positive(
 962                            Hilla_kminus1, Vmax=Vmax_b.unsqueeze(0), A=0,
 963                            K=K_b.unsqueeze(0), n=n_b.unsqueeze(0),
 964                            epsilon=epsilon_tensor
 965                        )  # [N, T, K-1]
 966                        combined_hill = alpha.unsqueeze(0) * Hillb_kminus1  # [N, T, K-1]
 967                        y_kminus1 = A_kminus1_expanded + combined_hill      # [N, T, K-1]
 968
 969                    # Clamp K-1 probabilities to [epsilon, 1-epsilon] to ensure valid residual
 970                    y_kminus1 = torch.clamp(y_kminus1, min=epsilon_tensor, max=1.0 - epsilon_tensor)
 971
 972                    # Ensure sum of K-1 doesn't exceed 1
 973                    sum_kminus1 = y_kminus1.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)  # [N, T, 1]
 974                    # If sum > (1-epsilon), rescale proportionally
 975                    y_kminus1 = torch.where(
 976                        sum_kminus1 > (1.0 - epsilon_tensor),
 977                        y_kminus1 * (1.0 - epsilon_tensor) / sum_kminus1,
 978                        y_kminus1
 979                    )
 980
 981                    # Compute Kth category as residual: y_K = 1 - sum(y_1, ..., y_{K-1})
 982                    y_K = 1.0 - y_kminus1.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)  # [N, T, 1]
 983                    y_K = torch.clamp(y_K, min=epsilon_tensor, max=1.0 - epsilon_tensor)
 984
 985                    # Concatenate to get all K probabilities
 986                    y_dose_response = torch.cat([y_kminus1, y_K], dim=-1)  # [N, T, K]
 987
 988                else:
 989                    # For non-multinomial: standard Hill computation
 990                    if distribution == 'binomial':
 991                        # For binomial: use log_K_a/log_K_b (numerically stable sigmoid formulation)
 992                        # y = A + (alpha * Hill_a(Vmax=Vmax_a)) + (beta * Hill_b(Vmax=Vmax_b))
 993                        # Note: Vmax_a + Vmax_b CAN exceed 1 - we'll try without clamp first
 994
 995                        if function_type == 'single_hill':
 996                            Hilla = Hill_based_positive_logK(x_true.unsqueeze(-1), Vmax=Vmax_a, A=0, logK=log_K_a, n=n_a)
 997                            y_dose_response = A + (alpha * Hilla)
 998
 999                        elif function_type == 'additive_hill':
1000                            Hilla = Hill_based_positive_logK(x_true.unsqueeze(-1), Vmax=Vmax_a, A=0, logK=log_K_a, n=n_a)
1001                            Hillb = Hill_based_positive_logK(x_true.unsqueeze(-1), Vmax=Vmax_b, A=0, logK=log_K_b, n=n_b)
1002                            y_dose_response = A + (alpha * Hilla) + (beta * Hillb)
1003
1004                        elif function_type == 'nested_hill':
1005                            Hilla = Hill_based_positive_logK(x_true.unsqueeze(-1), Vmax=Vmax_a, A=0, logK=log_K_a, n=n_a)
1006                            Hillb = Hill_based_positive(Hilla, Vmax=Vmax_b, A=0, K=K_b, n=n_b, epsilon=epsilon_tensor)
1007                            y_dose_response = A + (alpha * Hillb)
1008
1009                        # OPTIONAL CLAMP (commented out for now - try without first):
1010                        # If Vmax_a + Vmax_b > 1 causes issues, uncomment:
1011                        # y_dose_response = torch.clamp(y_dose_response, min=epsilon_tensor, max=1.0 - epsilon_tensor)
1012
1013                    else:
1014                        # For negbinom/normal/studentt: log_K_a/b are always available
1015                        # (log-normal prior is now the only path), so always use logK variant.
1016                        if function_type == 'single_hill':
1017                            Hilla = Hill_based_positive_logK(x_true.unsqueeze(-1), Vmax=Vmax_a, A=0, logK=log_K_a, n=n_a)
1018                            y_dose_response = A + (alpha * Hilla)
1019                        elif function_type == 'additive_hill':
1020                            Hilla = Hill_based_positive_logK(x_true.unsqueeze(-1), Vmax=Vmax_a, A=0, logK=log_K_a, n=n_a)
1021                            Hillb = Hill_based_positive_logK(x_true.unsqueeze(-1), Vmax=Vmax_b, A=0, logK=log_K_b, n=n_b)
1022                            y_dose_response = A + (alpha * Hilla) + (beta * Hillb)
1023                        elif function_type == 'nested_hill':
1024                            Hilla = Hill_based_positive_logK(x_true.unsqueeze(-1), Vmax=Vmax_a, A=0, logK=log_K_a, n=n_a)
1025                            Hillb = Hill_based_positive_logK(Hilla, Vmax=Vmax_b, A=0, logK=log_K_b, n=n_b)
1026                            y_dose_response = A + (alpha * Hillb)
1027
1028            elif function_type == 'polynomial':
1029                assert polynomial_degree is not None and polynomial_degree >= 1, \
1030                    "polynomial_degree must be ≥ 1 (no intercept, A is handled separately)"
1031
1032                if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None:
1033                    # For multinomial: fit K independent polynomials (one per category) in logit space
1034                    # Then apply softmax to get K probabilities that sum to 1
1035                    # This is more standard than K-1 with residual for unbounded logit space
1036
1037                    # Sample per-category polynomial coefficients
1038                    coeffs_per_category = []
1039                    for d in range(1, polynomial_degree + 1):
1040                        with pyro.plate(f"poly_category_plate_deg{d}", K, dim=-2):
1041                            coeff = pyro.sample(f"poly_coeff_{d}", dist.Normal(0., sigma_coeff))  # [K, T]
1042                            coeffs_per_category.append(coeff)
1043                    coeffs = torch.stack(coeffs_per_category, dim=-3)  # [degree, K, T]
1044
1045                    if latents_only:
1046                        return
1047
1048                    # Compute polynomial for each category
1049                    # coeffs: [degree, K, T]
1050                    # Need to permute to [degree, T, K] for Polynomial_function to work correctly
1051                    coeffs_permuted = coeffs.permute(0, 2, 1)  # [degree, T, K]
1052                    poly_val = Polynomial_function(x_true_sample, coeffs_permuted)  # [N, T, K]
1053
1054                    # A is baseline logit for each category (need K logits)
1055                    # Sample K baseline logits (unbounded)
1056                    with pyro.plate("category_plate_A", K, dim=-2):
1057                        A_clamped = torch.clamp(A.unsqueeze(-2), min=epsilon_tensor, max=1.0 - epsilon_tensor)  # [1, T]
1058                        logit_A_transpose = torch.log(A_clamped) - torch.log(1 - A_clamped)  # [K, T] logits
1059                    logit_A = logit_A_transpose.transpose(-1, -2)  # [T, K]
1060
1061                    # Compute logits for each category
1062                    logits_K = logit_A.unsqueeze(0) + alpha.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(-1) * poly_val  # [N, T, K]
1063
1064                    # Apply softmax to get probabilities that sum to 1
1065                    y_dose_response = torch.softmax(logits_K, dim=-1)  # [N, T, K]
1066
1067                else:
1068                    # For non-multinomial: single set of coefficients per feature
1069                    # Stack polynomial coefficients
1070                    coeffs = []
1071                    for d in range(1, polynomial_degree + 1):  # start at degree 1, no intercept
1072                        coeff = pyro.sample(f"poly_coeff_{d}", dist.Normal(0., sigma_coeff))
1073                        coeffs.append(coeff)
1074                    coeffs = torch.stack(coeffs, dim=-2)  # [degree, T]
1075                    if (coeffs.shape[1] == 1) & (coeffs.ndim == 4):
1076                        coeffs = coeffs.squeeze(1)        # [S, D, T]
1077
1078                    if latents_only:
1079                        return
1080
1081                    # Distribution-specific polynomial computation:
1082                    if distribution in ['normal', 'studentt']:
1083                        # For continuous distributions: work in natural space (no logs!)
1084                        # Polynomial is applied to x_true directly: y = A + alpha * poly(x)
1085                        poly_val = Polynomial_function(x_true_sample, coeffs)  # [N, T]
1086                        y_dose_response = A + alpha * poly_val  # [N, T] - can be negative!
1087
1088                    elif distribution in ['negbinom']:
1089                        # For negbinom: work in log space
1090                        # Polynomial is applied to log2(x): log2(y) = log2(A) + alpha * poly(log2(x))
1091                        log2_x_true = torch.log2(x_true_sample)  # [N]
1092                        poly_val = Polynomial_function(log2_x_true, coeffs)  # [N, T]
1093                        log2_y_dose_response = torch.log2(A) + alpha * poly_val  # [N, T]
1094                        y_dose_response = 2 ** log2_y_dose_response  # Convert back to count space
1095
1096                    elif distribution == 'binomial':
1097                        # For binomial: work in LOGIT space (unbounded: -inf to +inf)
1098                        # A is in [0,1] from Beta prior, convert to logit
1099                        # Polynomial is applied to x_true: logit(p) = logit(A) + alpha * poly(x)
1100                        A_clamped = torch.clamp(A, min=epsilon_tensor, max=1.0 - epsilon_tensor)
1101                        logit_A = torch.log(A_clamped) - torch.log(1 - A_clamped)  # logit(A)
1102                        poly_val = Polynomial_function(x_true_sample, coeffs)  # [N, T]
1103                        logit_p = logit_A + alpha * poly_val  # [N, T] - logit space (unbounded)
1104                        # Convert back to probability space for sampler
1105                        y_dose_response = torch.sigmoid(logit_p)  # [N, T] in [0, 1]
1106
1107                    else:
1108                        raise ValueError(f"Unknown distribution for polynomial: {distribution}")
1109            else:
1110                raise ValueError(f"Unknown function_type: {function_type}")
1111            
1112
1113        ##########################
1114        ## Cell-level variables ##
1115        ##########################
1116        # At this point, y_dose_response contains the dose-response function output.
1117        # We need to transform it to the format expected by samplers.
1118        #
1119        # IMPORTANT: Samplers in distributions.py handle technical group effects themselves!
1120        # Do NOT apply alpha_y here - pass it to the sampler via alpha_y_full.
1121
1122        # Prepare alpha_y_full (full C technical groups, including reference)
1123        # This will be passed to samplers, which apply technical groups themselves
1124        # Multinomial now supported (additive on logit scale, like binomial)
1125        if alpha_y is not None and groups_tensor is not None:
1126            # CRITICAL: Check if alpha_y already includes reference group
1127            # If alpha_y.shape[0 or 1] == C, it already has reference, don't add it!
1128
1129            if alpha_y.dim() == 4:  # Predictive multinomial: Could be (S, C-1, T, K) or (S, C, T, K)
1130                if alpha_y.shape[1] == C:
1131                    # Already includes reference
1132                    alpha_y_full = alpha_y
1133                else:
1134                    # Need to add reference (zeros for additive on logit scale)
1135                    baseline_shape = (alpha_y.shape[0], 1, alpha_y.shape[2], alpha_y.shape[3])
1136                    baseline = torch.zeros(baseline_shape, device=self.model.device)
1137                    alpha_y_full = torch.cat([baseline, alpha_y], dim=1)
1138
1139            elif alpha_y.dim() == 3:
1140                # Could be Predictive 2D (S, C-1, T) or Training multinomial (C-1, T, K) or (C, T, K)
1141                # Check if last dimension matches K (multinomial) or T (2D predictive)
1142                if distribution == 'multinomial' and K is not None and alpha_y.shape[-1] == K:
1143                    # Training multinomial: (C-1, T, K) or (C, T, K)
1144                    if alpha_y.shape[0] == C:
1145                        # Already includes reference
1146                        alpha_y_full = alpha_y
1147                    else:
1148                        # Need to add reference (zeros for additive on logit scale)
1149                        baseline_shape = (1, alpha_y.shape[1], alpha_y.shape[2])
1150                        baseline = torch.zeros(baseline_shape, device=self.model.device)
1151                        alpha_y_full = torch.cat([baseline, alpha_y], dim=0)
1152                else:
1153                    # Predictive 2D: (S, C-1, T) or (S, C, T)
1154                    if alpha_y.shape[1] == C:
1155                        # Already includes reference
1156                        alpha_y_full = alpha_y
1157                    else:
1158                        # Need to add reference (zeros for additive, ones for multiplicative)
1159                        ones_shape = (alpha_y.shape[0], 1, T)
1160                        if distribution == 'negbinom':
1161                            baseline = torch.ones(ones_shape, device=self.model.device)
1162                        else:
1163                            baseline = torch.zeros(ones_shape, device=self.model.device)
1164                        alpha_y_full = torch.cat([baseline, alpha_y], dim=1)
1165
1166            elif alpha_y.dim() == 2:  # Training 2D: Could be (C-1, T) or (C, T)
1167                if alpha_y.shape[0] == C:
1168                    # Already includes reference
1169                    alpha_y_full = alpha_y
1170                else:
1171                    # Need to add reference (zeros for additive, ones for multiplicative)
1172                    ones_shape = (1, T)
1173                    if distribution == 'negbinom':
1174                        baseline = torch.ones(ones_shape, device=self.model.device)
1175                    else:
1176                        baseline = torch.zeros(ones_shape, device=self.model.device)
1177                    alpha_y_full = torch.cat([baseline, alpha_y], dim=0)
1178            else:
1179                raise ValueError(f"Unexpected alpha_y shape: {alpha_y.shape}")
1180        else:

1189
1190        elif distribution == 'binomial':

1200            # Zero out phantom categories so _masked_softmax in sample_multinomial_trans

1209

1211            raise ValueError(f"Unknown distribution: {distribution}")

1216            check_tensor("y_dose_response", y_dose_response)

1218            check_tensor("phi_y_used", phi_y_used)
1219            check_tensor("A", A)

1222                check_tensor("Vmax_a", Vmax_a)
1223                check_tensor("K_a", K_a)
1224            if function_type in ['additive_hill', 'nested_hill']:

1227                check_tensor("K_b", K_b)
1228            if function_type == 'polynomial':
1229                check_tensor("coeffs", coeffs)
1230
1231        # Call distribution-specific observation sampler
1232        from .distributions import get_observation_sampler
1233        observation_sampler = get_observation_sampler(distribution, 'trans')
1234
1235        # Call the appropriate sampler based on distribution
1236        if distribution == 'negbinom':

1238                y_obs_tensor=y_obs_tensor,
1239                mu_y=mu_y,

1241                alpha_y_full=alpha_y_full,
1242                groups_tensor=groups_tensor,
1243                sum_factor_tensor=sum_factor_tensor,

1245                T=T,
1246                C=C,
1247                use_epsilon=use_epsilon
1248            )

1256                N=N,
1257                T=T,
1258                K=K,
1259                C=C

1263                y_obs_tensor=y_obs_tensor,
1264                denominator_tensor=denominator_tensor,
1265                mu_y=mu_y,  # Should be probabilities [N, T]
1266                alpha_y_full=alpha_y_full,
1267                groups_tensor=groups_tensor,
1268                N=N,
1269                T=T,
1270                C=C
1271            )

1274                y_obs_tensor=y_obs_tensor,
